properties.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
properties.style: Mesolithic hunting scenes, dancing figures, animals in red ochre and white; later Chalcolithic and historic layers
properties.discovery: 1957, V.S. Wakankar (spotted from a passing train)
properties.summary: India's largest and most famous concentration of prehistoric rock art, with over 700 shelters in Vindhyan sandstone hills south of Bhopal. Paintings span the Mesolithic through the medieval period, showing hunting parties, dancers, boar-like mythical beasts and processions of horse riders. Occupation deposits go back to the Acheulian, making it a continuous record of human life for over 100,000 years.
properties.notes: Painting dates debated: most art is Mesolithic (c. 10000-2000 BCE) but some scholars claim origins up to 30,000 years ago; cupules in Auditorium Cave may be far older.

properties.name: Jogimara and Sitabenga Caves (Ramgarh Hill)
properties.style: Early historic polychrome frescoes (dancers, elephants, fish) with Brahmi/Magadhi inscriptions; adjacent rock-cut 'theatre' cave
properties.discovery: Documented 1904-05 by T. Bloch (ASI); inscriptions read earlier by Cunningham's surveys
properties.summary: On Ramgarh hill in Surguja district, Jogimara cave preserves what are among the oldest surviving painted murals in India, dated to the 3rd-1st century BCE. The neighbouring Sitabenga cave, with carved gallery seating, is often called the world's oldest surviving theatre. A famous Brahmi inscription records the love of Devadinna for the 'devadasi' Sutanuka.
properties.notes: These are early-historic murals rather than prehistoric rock art; a second cruder painting phase is some centuries later.

properties.name: Lakhudiyar Rock Shelter
properties.style: Black, red-ochre and white paintings: dancing human chains, wavy lines, geometric and animal motifs
properties.discovery: 1968, Dr. M.P. Joshi
properties.summary: A painted overhang ('one lakh caves') on the bank of the Suyal river near Barechhina, 19 km from Almora — the best-known rock art site of the Kumaon Himalaya. Its hand-linked dancing human figures and geometric patterns are a textbook image of Himalayan prehistoric art. Easily visited on the Almora-Seraghat road.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Barechhina village); absolute dating not established — attributions range from late Mesolithic to Chalcolithic.

properties.name: Chaturbhujnath Nala Rock Art Gallery
properties.style: Dense Mesolithic-Chalcolithic narrative panels: cattle herding, riders, dancing, hunting — one of the world's longest painted galleries
properties.discovery: 1977, Ramesh Kumar Pancholi (local schoolteacher)
properties.protection: State archaeology (within Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary)
properties.summary: Along a stream near Bhanpura in Mandsaur district, painted shelters run almost continuously for several kilometres, often called the longest rock art gallery in the world. Thousands of small, lively figures document the shift from hunting to cattle-keeping in the Chambal valley. The site sits inside Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary amid dramatic gorge scenery.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (nala mouth near Chaturbhujnath temple); popular claims of '35,000 years' are exaggerated — most panels are Mesolithic to Chalcolithic.

properties.name: Daraki-Chattan Cupule Cave
properties.style: Cupules (hemispherical cup-marks) pecked into quartzite — candidates for the world's oldest surviving rock art
properties.discovery: Reported 1990s; investigated 2002-2006 by Giriraj Kumar and Robert Bednarik (EIP Project)
properties.summary: A narrow quartzite cleft on Indragarh hill near Bhanpura containing over 500 cupules. Excavations recovered hammerstones in Lower Palaeolithic (Acheulian) deposits, leading researchers to argue these are among the earliest known examples of intentional rock markings by humans anywhere on Earth.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx. Acheulian age claim is internationally debated; even conservative estimates place the cupules in the Palaeolithic. Map display will clamp to -2000.

properties.name: Adamgarh Rock Shelters
properties.style: Mesolithic paintings of giraffe-like animals, hunters, riders; later historic figures
properties.discovery: 1922, Manoranjan Ghosh
properties.summary: Eighteen shelters on a low hill 2 km south of Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram) overlooking the Narmada river, one of the first Indian rock art sites to be scientifically excavated. Eleven shelters still show paintings of animals, hunters and riders, with microlithic tool deposits beneath. Radiocarbon dates from Adamgarh anchored the chronology of the Indian Mesolithic.
properties.notes: Most visible paintings are Chalcolithic to early historic; only a few securely Mesolithic panels survive.

properties.name: Pachmarhi Hills Rock Shelters (Mahadeo Hills)
properties.style: Mesolithic to historic paintings: hunters, honey collection, battle scenes, in white and red ochre
properties.discovery: Documented from 1930s (D.H. Gordon); studied extensively by V.S. Wakankar and later scholars
properties.protection: State archaeology (within Satpura Tiger Reserve / UNESCO Biosphere Reserve)
properties.summary: Dozens of painted shelters — Dhuandhar, Nimbu Bhoj, Dorothy Deep, Jambu Dwip, Bazaar Cave among them — dot the sandstone ravines of the Pachmarhi plateau in the Satpura range. The art spans hunter-gatherer scenes of the Mesolithic through medieval battle processions. Combined with waterfalls and forest trails, it is the most accessible rock art landscape in central India after Bhimbetka.
properties.notes: Coordinates are for Pachmarhi town; shelters are scattered across the surrounding hills. Dating is stylistic, not absolute.

properties.name: Kupgal / Hiregudda (Kappagallu) Petroglyphs
properties.style: Neolithic petroglyphs — bruised humped cattle, human figures — on dolerite; associated 'rock gong' musical boulders
properties.discovery: First reported 1892 (colonial period); rediscovered and studied from 2002 by Nicole Boivin and team
properties.summary: On Hiregudda ('Peacock Hill') near Ballari, thousands of pecked images of long-horned cattle and humans cover a granite-dolerite ridge above Neolithic ash mounds. Certain boulders ring musically when struck, suggesting the hill was a ritual soundscape for South India's first herders. It is among the richest Neolithic petroglyph sites in the subcontinent.
properties.notes: Neolithic activity radiocarbon-dated c. 2000-1200 BCE, but imagery accumulated over several millennia into the historic period. Threatened by granite quarrying.

properties.name: Onake Kindi Rock Shelters (Anegundi)
properties.style: Neolithic-Iron Age paintings in red and white: bulls, concentric circles, hunters on horseback, a famous 'spoked wheel' sun motif
properties.discovery: Documented in surveys of the Hampi-Anegundi region (late 20th century)
properties.protection: Unprotected (within Hampi World Heritage buffer landscape)
properties.summary: Hidden among the granite boulder hills of Anegundi, across the Tungabhadra from Hampi, Onake Kindi's shelters carry striking red-and-white paintings of cattle, wheels and mounted hunters. Together with nearby megalithic burials it records the Neolithic-to-Iron Age transition of the Deccan. A short walk from Chikkarampur village makes it an easy add-on to a Hampi visit.
properties.notes: Dating is stylistic (roughly 1500 BCE - early historic); site is on private farmland, unsigned.

properties.name: Edakkal Caves
properties.style: Deeply incised Neolithic petroglyphs: anthropomorphs with headdresses, wheeled carts, geometric signs; early Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions
properties.discovery: 1890s, Fred Fawcett (Malabar police superintendent), published 1901
properties.summary: Two natural fissure-caves high on Ambukuthi hill in Wayanad, whose walls are covered with some of South India's finest prehistoric engravings — stylised human figures, animals and symbols cut into the rock over several millennia. Later visitors added inscriptions, including one linked to the Chera king. The climb rewards with sweeping views over the Wayanad plateau.
properties.notes: Engraving phases range from Neolithic (claims to 6000 BCE) to early historic; precise dating unresolved.

properties.name: Ezhuthupara (Marayoor / Anjanad Valley)
properties.style: Red-ochre, white and yellow pictographs: human figures with raised hands, bulls, deer, palm impressions
properties.discovery: Documented by Kerala archaeology; Anjanad valley surveys have recorded ~20 painted shelters
properties.protection: State archaeology (Kerala; within Koodakkadu sandalwood reserve)
properties.summary: The Anjanad valley around Marayoor in Idukki holds Kerala's largest cluster of painted rock shelters, with Ezhuthupara ('writing rock') the best known — a serpent-hood shaped granite overhang bearing dozens of ochre figures. Nearby Attala shelter has over 90 mostly abstract motifs. The paintings sit amid Marayoor's famous dolmens and sandalwood forests.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx. Attribution ranges from Mesolithic to Megalithic Iron Age; access to some shelters requires forest permission.

properties.name: Unakoti Rock-Cut Sculptures
properties.style: Colossal rock-cut bas-reliefs — 9 m Shiva head (Unakotisvara Kal Bhairava), Ganesha, Durga — carved into a forested hillside
properties.discovery: Long-known Shaivite pilgrimage site; documented by ASI in the 20th century
properties.summary: Legend says 99,99,999 gods were turned to stone here, giving Unakoti ('one less than a crore') its name. Enormous 7th-9th century CE faces of Shiva and other deities are hewn directly from the hillside beside waterfalls in Kailashahar's forests. It is the premier rock-carving site of Northeast India and an active pilgrimage centre during Ashokastami Mela.
properties.notes: Historic-period rock carving, not prehistoric — included for its rock-cut art significance; dating (600-900 CE) is stylistic.

properties.name: Konkan Geoglyphs (Barsu-Kasheli-Ukshi cluster, Ratnagiri)
properties.style: Petroglyphs/geoglyphs cut into laterite plateaus: an 18 m elephant filled with 70+ animals (Kasheli), 'master of animals' panel (Barsu), sharks, stingrays, abstract labyrinths
properties.discovery: Systematically documented from 2012 onward by Sudhir Risbud, Dhananjay Marathe and the 'Konkan Taka' explorers
properties.protection: State archaeology; on UNESCO tentative list (2022) — sites at Ukshi, Jambharun, Kasheli, Rundhe Tali, Devihsol, Barsu, Devache Gothane
properties.summary: Across the flat laterite plateaus of coastal Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg, over 1,500 large rock engravings ('katal shilpa') at 70+ villages depict elephants, tigers, marine creatures and enigmatic geometric designs, some visible only from above. Attributed to Mesolithic hunter-gatherers, they include the largest rock engravings in India. Barsu and Kasheli are the flagship sites.
properties.notes: Cluster coordinates approx (Barsu plateau, Rajapur taluka). Age estimates of 10,000-20,000 BP are stylistic/geological, not radiometric; some sites threatened by proposed refinery.

properties.name: Ambadevi Rock Shelters (Gawilgarh Hills)
properties.style: Petroglyphs, pictograms, cupules and geometric motifs in sandstone shelters of the Satpura-Tapti valley
properties.discovery: 2007, Vijay Ingole and team
properties.summary: A 40 sq km complex of over 100 shelters in the Gawilgarh hills north of Amravati, around the Ambadevi and Salbardi cave temples, discovered only in 2007. Thirty shelters carry paintings, engravings and cupules that researchers argue reach back some 25,000 years. It is Vidarbha's most important prehistoric art landscape.
properties.notes: The claimed Upper Palaeolithic age awaits absolute dating; site straddles the Maharashtra-Madhya Pradesh (Betul) border.

properties.name: Usgalimal (Pansaimol) Rock Engravings
properties.style: Laterite petroglyphs: bulls, deer, peacocks, a spiral labyrinth, 'mother goddess' and dancing figures
properties.discovery: 1993, exposed by monsoon flood of the Kushavati river; documented by Goa Directorate of Archives & Archaeology
properties.summary: On the bank of the Kushavati river in Sanguem taluka, more than 100 figures are carved into a sloping sheet of laterite — Goa's most important prehistoric monument. Highlights include a large labyrinth spiral and composite animal-human scenes attributed to Mesolithic-Neolithic hunter-fisher communities. A riverside forest setting makes it an atmospheric detour from South Goa.
properties.notes: Dating estimates range from Mesolithic (8000+ BP) to Neolithic (4000-6000 BP); no absolute dates.

properties.name: Kilvalai (Keezhvalai) Rock Paintings
properties.style: Red-ochre and white kaolin paintings: bird-headed anthropomorphs, riders, cattle, hunting scenes of the Iron Age/megalithic period
properties.discovery: Documented by Tamil Nadu State Archaeology Department (reported from the 1980s onward)
properties.summary: In boulder shelters near Kandachipuram, 24 km northwest of Villupuram, Kilvalai preserves the best-known rock paintings of northern Tamil Nadu — strange bird-headed human figures, animals and riders painted around 3,000 years ago. It anchors a cluster of painted sites (Settavarai, Alambadi, Udayanatham) along the Thenpennai valley.
properties.notes: Megalithic-period attribution (c. 1000 BCE) is stylistic; some panels use white kaolin over earlier red figures.

properties.name: Settavarai Rock Paintings
properties.style: White kaolin and red-ochre animal figures, deer hunts and geometric symbols on granite shelters
properties.discovery: Documented by Tamil Nadu State Archaeology Department
properties.summary: Near Gingee in Villupuram district, the boulder hill at Settavarai carries megalithic-era paintings dominated by animal imagery — deer, cattle and hunters — executed mostly in white pigment. Together with Kilvalai it forms the core of Tamil Nadu's most accessible rock art circuit, about 40 km from Villupuram town.
properties.notes: Dating stylistic (c. 1000 BCE - early historic).

properties.name: Karikkiyur (Porivarai) Rock Art
properties.style: Over 300 painted images across a 100 m frieze: hunters, wild cattle, dancing scenes tracing the shift from foraging to herding
properties.discovery: Known to local Irula community; brought to scholarly notice in the 20th century, restudied 2000s-2020s
properties.protection: Unprotected (sacred site of the Irula community)
properties.summary: The east-facing Porivarai shelter near Karikkiyur village, Kotagiri, is the largest rock painting site in Tamil Nadu — a 150 m long rock face in the Nilgiri escarpment bearing more than 300 figures. The imagery moves from hunting scenes to cattle and settled life, and the shelter remains sacred to the Irula people, whose Kurumba neighbours continue related painting traditions.
properties.notes: No absolute dates; estimates range c. 8000-2700 BCE for earliest phases. Access is a forest trek requiring local guidance.

properties.name: Alaniya Rock Shelters (Chambal Valley)
properties.style: Mesolithic-Chalcolithic red-ochre paintings: deer, bulls, hunters, geometric designs along the Alaniya river gorge
properties.discovery: Region first explored by V.S. Wakankar (Dara, 1953); Alaniya documented in subsequent Chambal surveys
properties.protection: State archaeology; part of 'Rock Art Sites of the Chambal Valley' UNESCO tentative list
properties.summary: Near Alaniya dam south of Kota, painted sandstone shelters line a tributary gorge of the Chambal with animal and hunting imagery dated as far back as c. 5000 BCE. The site belongs to a belt of some 3,000 reported rock shelters in southeastern Rajasthan, the state's richest prehistoric art region.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Alaniya village/dam area). Dates are stylistic estimates.

properties.name: Gararda / Bundi Rock Painting Cluster
properties.style: Mesolithic red-ochre deer, bison, human figures across 100+ shelters along Chambal tributaries (Bijolia-Banki belt)
properties.discovery: 1997 onward, Om Prakash 'Kukki' Sharma (self-taught explorer, 100+ sites)
properties.summary: Around Bundi and Gararda, over a hundred painted shelters hug the ravines of the Mangli and other Chambal tributaries, discovered largely by local enthusiast 'Kukki' Sharma. Estimated at up to 15,000 years old, the vivid ochre deer, bison and stick-figure hunters make Bundi a rewarding off-beat rock art safari from the famous stepwell town.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Gararda area). The 15,000-year age is a stylistic claim without absolute dating.

properties.name: Zawar Rock Art (Tiri-Zawar, Aravalli belt)
properties.style: Red-ochre paintings of animals and human figures in shelters of the Aravalli hills near the ancient Zawar zinc mines
properties.discovery: Documented in Mewar-region rock art surveys (V.S. Wakankar and later Rajasthan Vidyapeeth teams)
properties.summary: South of Udaipur, the hills around Zawar — famous for the world's oldest industrial zinc smelting — also hold painted rock shelters attributed to Chalcolithic and later communities of the Banas-Aravalli culture zone. The pairing of prehistoric art with a landmark of early metallurgy makes this a distinctive heritage stop in Mewar.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Zawar mines area). Documentation is thin; dating highly uncertain — treat period as indicative.

properties.name: Domkhar Rock Art Sanctuary
properties.style: Bronze Age 'animal style' petroglyphs — ibex, yaks, hunters, mascoids — pecked on river boulders, with Central Asian steppe affinities
properties.discovery: Long known locally; sanctuary created 2012 by villagers with researcher support
properties.summary: On the Indus riverbank at Domkhar Dho, 112 km from Leh on the Sham valley road, hundreds of dark boulders carry elegant petroglyphs of ibex, yaks and hunters, some in the Eurasian steppe 'animal style' dated to around 3000 BCE. A village-run sanctuary protects the finest concentration of Ladakh's estimated 20,000+ petroglyphs.
properties.notes: Dating comparative (Bronze Age to early historic); many Ladakh petroglyph sites elsewhere have been lost to road-building.

properties.name: Murgi (Nubra) Petroglyph Field
properties.style: Over 3,000 pecked carvings — ibex, hunting scenes, caravans, Buddhist symbols — Ladakh's largest single petroglyph site
properties.discovery: Documented in Nubra valley surveys (Laurianne Bruneau and others, 2000s)
properties.summary: Near Murgi and Panamik in the Nubra valley, along the old caravan route to the Karakoram passes, boulder fields carry more than 3,000 carvings spanning the Bronze Age to the Buddhist era. The site records millennia of herders, hunters and Silk Route travellers writing on stone at the edge of the high Karakoram.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Murgi village near Panamik). Chronology spans prehistory to historic; no formal protection.

properties.name: Burzahom (Neolithic hunting-scene engraving)
properties.style: Neolithic stone-slab engraving of a stag hunt with archer, spearman, dog and twin 'suns' — Kashmir's oldest artwork
properties.discovery: Site found 1935 (H. de Terra & T.T. Paterson); excavated 1960-71 by ASI (T.N. Khazanchi), when the engraved slabs were recovered
properties.summary: The Neolithic pit-dwelling settlement of Burzahom near Srinagar yielded a famous engraved slab showing hunters spearing a stag beneath two radiant discs — often read as a depiction of a sky event. It is the earliest known art of the Kashmir valley and a touchstone for Neolithic life on the karewa plateaus above Dal Lake.
properties.notes: The engraving is an excavated artifact from the site rather than an in-situ rock panel; dated to Neolithic phase II (c. 3rd millennium BCE).

properties.name: Bomai Petroglyphs (Sopore)
properties.style: Pecked concentric circles, star clusters (possibly Orion), chase scenes and schematic humans on boulders near Wular lake
properties.discovery: Reported 2000s by University of Kashmir researchers (Mumtaz Yatoo and colleagues)
properties.summary: At Bomai near Sopore, boulders above the Wular lake basin carry Kashmir's only known open-air petroglyphs, attributed to the Neolithic around 2000 BCE. Some researchers read one cluster of cup-marks as an early star map of the Orion constellation, linking the carvings to ancient sky-watching in the valley.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Bomai village). Astronomical interpretation is speculative; dating comparative.

properties.name: Gudahandi Rock Shelters
properties.style: Red and polychrome pictographs: stylised humans, deer, grids, wheels and geometric patterns on 'pot-shaped' hills
properties.discovery: Documented in Odisha archaeology surveys (reported from the 1970s-80s)
properties.summary: In the Ampani hills of Kalahandi district, the paired dome-shaped hills of Gudahandi ('pot of treasure') shelter red and black geometric paintings and animal figures at the mouths of natural caves. They are among the oldest painted images in eastern India, set in a scenic sanctuary landscape near the Nabarangpur border.
properties.notes: Popular claims of 20,000-25,000 BP are unverified; scholarly estimates favour Mesolithic to Chalcolithic. Site is remote (about 17 km from Ampani).

properties.name: Yogimatha Rock Painting
properties.style: Neolithic red-ochre frieze of a humped bull with cow, calf and human figure — an icon of early animal domestication
properties.discovery: Documented in Nuapada district surveys (20th century)
properties.summary: Nine kilometres from Khariar in Nuapada district, the Yogimatha shelter bears a celebrated Neolithic painting of a bull, cow, calf and herder — read as one of India's earliest depictions of animal domestication. The forested sandstone outcrop is also a local pilgrimage spot.
properties.notes: Traditional claims place it as early as the 10th millennium BCE; Neolithic (c. 4th-2nd millennium BCE) is more widely accepted.

properties.name: Sitabhinji Rock Shelters (Ravana Chhaya)
properties.style: Gupta-period tempera mural: royal procession with king Disabhanja on elephant, in white, buff, brown, red and yellow ochre
properties.discovery: Documented 1940s-50s (noted by ASI scholars including T.N. Ramachandran)
properties.summary: Beneath the half-dome boulder called Ravana Chhaya near Danguapasi in Keonjhar district survives one of India's rarest early tempera paintings outside Ajanta — a 5th-6th century CE royal procession with an inscription naming Maharaja Disabhanja. Surrounding shelters hold inscriptions, sculptures and the remains of an ancient settlement.
properties.notes: Historic-period mural on a natural rock shelter, included as a bridge between prehistoric rock art and classical painting.

properties.name: Pandavula Gutta
properties.style: Mesolithic to medieval paintings in green, red, yellow and white: bison, antelope, tiger, swastika and geometric signs
properties.discovery: 1990, K. Ramakrishna Rao and S.S. Rangacharyulu (ASI Hyderabad)
properties.protection: State archaeology (Heritage Telangana); declared Telangana's first geo-heritage site (2024)
properties.summary: A sandstone hill complex near Regonda in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, said to be geologically older than the Himalaya, whose shelters carry paintings from Mesolithic hunters through medieval Jain and Kakatiya-era art. Wild animals, weapons and symbols in multiple pigments make it Telangana's richest rock art destination.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Kothapally/Regonda area). Habitation span cited as c. 20,500-4,000 years ago; individual panel dates uncertain.

properties.name: Chintakunta Rock Shelters
properties.style: About 200 Mesolithic red and white line paintings: deer, humped bulls, elephants, hyenas, anthropomorphs and geometric designs
properties.discovery: Recognised 1981 as South India's first major Mesolithic line-painting site
properties.summary: On an Erramala hill spur near Muddanur in Kadapa district, ten shelters and fifteen painted boulders make Chintakunta one of India's largest rock art sites after Bhimbetka. Its red and white line paintings of wild animals and hunters document Mesolithic life on the southern Deccan.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (7 km SW of Muddanur on Tadipatri-Renigunta road). Dating stylistic (c. 8000-1500 BCE).

properties.name: Ketavaram (Kethavaram) Rock Paintings
properties.style: Red-ochre paintings in 10 of 13 shelters: deer, hyena, monkey, humped bulls, tiger, lizards and human figures
properties.discovery: Documented in Kurnool district rock art surveys (published 2010s)
properties.summary: About 18 km from Kurnool on the Srisailam road, the quartzite shelters of Kethavaram overlook the Tungabhadra plain with paintings dominated by deer and wild animals. The Kurnool caves region has yielded some of India's oldest evidence of symbolic behaviour, and Kethavaram is its most visitable painted site.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx. Claims of 35,000-40,000 BP relate to regional Palaeolithic context; paintings themselves are likely Mesolithic and later.

properties.name: Isko (Isco) Rock Art
properties.style: Meso-Chalcolithic pictographs, over 90% non-figurative: lattices, mandala-like symbols echoed in living Adivasi khovar/sohrai wall art
properties.discovery: Brought to wider notice 1991 by Bulu Imam (INTACH Hazaribagh)
properties.summary: Above Isko village in the Barkagaon valley of Hazaribagh, a long sandstone shelter is covered in enigmatic geometric symbols attributed to the Meso-Chalcolithic (c. 9000-5000 BCE). Local Munda, Birhor and Oraon traditions of painted houses are strikingly similar, making Isko a living link between prehistoric and tribal art. The valley faces coal-mining pressure.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (published coordinates in one paper are erroneous). Dating relative, based on associated tools.

properties.name: Likhaniya Dari (Lakhaniya) Rock Shelters
properties.style: Mesolithic red-ochre paintings of hunters, animals and dancing figures beside a 150 m waterfall gorge
properties.discovery: Mirzapur region rock art first recorded 1867-68 by A.C.L. Carlleyle — among the earliest rock art discoveries in the world
properties.summary: The Likhaniya ('painted') gorge on the Garai river near Ahraura combines a spectacular seasonal waterfall with ochre paintings left by Mesolithic hunter-foragers of the Vindhya-Kaimur scarp. Mirzapur's painted shelters were noticed by Archibald Carlleyle in the 1860s, years before Altamira made rock art famous.
properties.notes: Name variants Likhaniya/Lakhaniya; several painted localities share the gorge. Dating stylistic.

properties.name: Wyndham Falls & Morhana Pahar Shelters (Mirzapur)
properties.style: Mesolithic paintings including the famous Morhana Pahar 'chariot' scene; hunters, animals and battle imagery
properties.discovery: Region documented from 1867-68 (A.C.L. Carlleyle); modern surveys by Ajay Pratap (BHU)
properties.summary: West of Mirzapur, painted shelters cluster around the Wyndham Falls picnic gorge and the Morhana escarpment on the old Grand Trunk alignment. Morhana Pahar's panel of a two-horse 'chariot' ambushed by bowmen is one of the most debated images in Indian rock art. The sites capture hunter-forager and pastoralist camps of the north Vindhyas.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Wyndham Falls); Morhana Pahar lies further south on the Mirzapur-Robertsganj road. Chariot panel likely early historic overlay on older art.

properties.name: Kaimur Range Rock Shelters (Mundeshwari hills area)
properties.style: Mesolithic and later paintings: humans, animals, trees, geometric and floral designs in 17+ shelters
properties.discovery: Explorations 1994-95 and later by Bihar archaeologists (Awadh Kishore Prasad and others)
properties.protection: Largely unprotected; near state-protected Mundeshwari temple
properties.summary: The Bihar stretch of the Kaimur plateau — around Bhagwanpur, Adhaura and the ancient Mundeshwari temple hill — holds at least 17 painted shelters above rivers and waterfalls. The art, likely 10,000 years old at its earliest, extends the great Vindhya-Kaimur rock art belt into Bihar and pairs well with a visit to India's oldest functioning temple.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Mundeshwari hill, Kaimur district); painted shelters are dispersed across the plateau. Dating relative.

properties.name: Mangar Bani Cave Paintings
properties.style: Paintings and cupules on Aravalli quartzite: human figurines, animals, foliage and geometric designs; associated Palaeolithic tools
properties.discovery: May-June 2021, Sunil Harsana (local ecologist) with Haryana Archaeology Department (Banani Bhattacharyya)
properties.protection: Unprotected (within sacred grove; protection notification pending)
properties.summary: In a sacred grove barely an hour from Delhi, the rocky ridges around Mangar Bani hide hundreds of painted panels and tool scatters announced in 2021 as potentially among India's oldest rock art. Preliminary study links the habitation to the Palaeolithic, with reuse continuing into the 8th-9th century CE — an astonishing survival on the capital's doorstep.
properties.notes: Claimed Upper Palaeolithic age of the paintings is provisional pending dating; tool evidence spans c. 100,000-15,000 BP. Coordinates are for Mangar Bani grove.

properties.name: Chamardi Rock Art
properties.style: Petroglyphs and painted panels including a rare Maitraka-period (6th-7th c. CE) scene of two sailing boats with helmsman and warriors
properties.discovery: Documented in Saurashtra rock art surveys (V.H. Sonawane and others)
properties.summary: Near Sihor in Bhavnagar district, the granite outcrops of Chamardi carry Gujarat's best-known rock art, famous for a painted panel of two sea-going boats from the Maitraka era — testimony to Saurashtra's ancient maritime world. Earlier engravings and cupules on the same hills point to prehistoric use.
properties.notes: Coordinates approx (Chamardi village). Gujarat's rock art record is sparse and thinly published; periods indicative only.

properties.name: Tabo-Lari Petroglyphs (Spiti Valley)
properties.style: Over 1,000 carved boulders: ibex, yaks, hunters, swastikas and Zhang Zhung-era symbols beside the Spiti river
properties.discovery: Documented 2015 by IGNCA field teams; earlier noted by Tibetologist John Bellezza
properties.summary: The lower Spiti valley around Tabo, Lari and Poh holds one of the densest petroglyph concentrations in the Tibetan cultural world — more than 1,000 carved boulders lying in the open beside the river. Ibex, hunters and pre-Buddhist symbols, some around 3,500 years old, complement a visit to the millennium-old Tabo monastery.
properties.notes: Coordinates are for Tabo; Lari boulder field lies a few km downstream. Many boulders lost to road widening; dating comparative.

properties.name: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya
properties.major_additions: present brick shikhara temple 5th-6th c. CE (Gupta); railings 1st c. BCE; restored 1880s
properties.style: early Nagara brick shikhara (Buddhist)
properties.summary: Marking the spot of the Buddha's enlightenment, this is one of the earliest surviving all-brick temples in India and the prototype of the straight-edged pyramidal tower. Its 55 m shikhara, largely of the Gupta period over an Ashokan core, shows Indian temple-tower design at the very moment of its birth.

properties.name: Barabar Caves (Lomas Rishi & Sudama)
properties.style: rock-cut (Mauryan)
properties.dynasty: Maurya (Ashoka and grandson Dasharatha), for Ajivika ascetics
properties.summary: India's oldest surviving rock-cut shrines, excavated under Emperor Ashoka with interiors polished to a mirror finish. The Lomas Rishi facade copies a wooden hut with a curved chaitya arch, the ancestor of a motif repeated on Indian temples for the next two thousand years.

properties.name: Great Stupa, Sanchi
properties.major_additions: enlarged with stone casing under Shungas 2nd c. BCE; four carved toranas 1st c. BCE (Satavahana)
properties.style: stupa (Buddhist)
properties.summary: Commissioned by Ashoka, the Great Stupa is the best-preserved monument of India's earliest structural sacred architecture. Its hemispherical dome, railed processional path and four sculpted gateways established the vocabulary of the stupa across Asia.

properties.name: Ajanta Caves
properties.major_additions: second great phase of chaityas, viharas and murals c. 460-480 CE under Vakataka king Harishena
properties.style: rock-cut (Buddhist chaitya and vihara)
properties.summary: Thirty caves cut into a horseshoe gorge trace Buddhist rock architecture from austere 2nd-century BCE prayer halls to the ornate pillared shrines of the 5th century CE. Their painted interiors are the finest surviving gallery of ancient Indian mural art.

properties.name: Udayagiri & Khandagiri Caves
properties.style: rock-cut (Jain monastic)
properties.summary: Carved for Jain monks under King Kharavela, these twin hills hold India's earliest major Jain rock-cut complex, including the double-storeyed Rani Gumpha. Their sculpted friezes and the Hathigumpha inscription make them a cornerstone of early Kalinga art.

properties.name: Karla Caves (Great Chaitya)
properties.major_additions: Great Chaitya hall completed c. 120 CE
properties.style: rock-cut (Buddhist chaitya)
properties.summary: The Great Chaitya at Karla is the largest and most perfectly finished early Buddhist prayer hall in India, its ribbed teak ceiling and colossal pillars faithfully translating timber construction into rock. It represents the climax of the Hinayana cave-temple tradition.

properties.name: Temple 17, Sanchi
properties.style: early Gupta flat-roofed structural temple
properties.summary: This small flat-roofed sanctum with a four-pillared porch is textbook 'temple number one' — among the first free-standing stone temples ever built in India. Its plain cubical cella defines the germ from which all later Nagara and Dravida temples grew.

properties.name: Udayagiri Caves (Vidisha)
properties.style: rock-cut (early Hindu)
properties.summary: Dated by inscription to Chandragupta II's reign, these caves contain the celebrated colossal Varaha rescuing the earth goddess — the first great statement of Hindu imperial iconography in stone. They mark the moment Hindu worship acquired monumental architectural form.

properties.name: Bhitargaon Brick Temple
properties.style: Gupta brick shikhara (proto-Nagara)
properties.summary: The oldest surviving terracotta-and-brick Hindu temple in India, Bhitargaon already carries a tall curved tower and true arches centuries before they became common. It is the crucial missing link between flat-roofed Gupta shrines and the soaring Nagara shikhara.

properties.name: Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh
properties.style: late Gupta early Nagara (panchayatana plan)
properties.summary: This Vishnu temple is the first known panchayatana-plan temple and one of the earliest with a stone shikhara, its doorway and Anantashayana relief ranking among the masterpieces of Gupta sculpture. It shows the fully formed classical temple emerging around 500 CE.
sources: Vats, The Gupta Temple at Deogarh (ASI Memoir)

properties.name: Durga Temple, Aihole
properties.style: early Chalukya experimental (apsidal with Nagara tower)
properties.summary: Aihole was the drawing board of Indian temple architecture, with over a hundred experimental shrines; its famous apsidal Durga Temple wraps a Buddhist chaitya plan in a Hindu colonnaded veranda. Here northern and southern temple ideas were tested side by side.
sources: UNESCO tentative list: Evolution of Temple Architecture, Aihole-Badami-Pattadakal

properties.name: Elephanta Caves
properties.style: rock-cut (Hindu, Shaiva)
properties.dynasty: Kalachuri / Konkan Mauryas (attributed to Krishnaraja I)
properties.summary: On an island in Mumbai harbour, the great cave of Shiva centres on the 6 m three-faced Sadashiva, one of the supreme achievements of Indian sculpture. Elephanta shows the Hindu cave temple at its most ambitious, a mandapa city carved from a single hill.

properties.name: Badami Cave Temples
properties.style: rock-cut (early Chalukya)
properties.summary: Four caves above a red sandstone gorge — three Hindu and one Jain — carry a dated inscription of 578 CE, making them a fixed point in the chronology of Deccan art. Their Nataraja with eighteen arms is an icon of early Chalukya sculpture.

properties.name: Ellora Caves (multi-faith complex)
properties.major_additions: Buddhist caves c. 600-730; Hindu caves 6th-9th c.; Jain caves 9th-10th c.
properties.style: rock-cut (Buddhist, Hindu, Jain)
properties.summary: Thirty-four monasteries and temples cut over four centuries into a two-kilometre basalt scarp, Ellora is the encyclopaedia of Indian rock architecture and of religious coexistence. It records the handover from Buddhist cave halls to Hindu and Jain temple forms.

properties.name: Pancha Rathas, Mahabalipuram
properties.style: monolithic rock-cut (proto-Dravida)
properties.summary: Five free-standing temples each carved from a single boulder, the rathas are a sculptor's catalogue of South Indian roof forms — from thatched hut to multi-storeyed vimana. They are the experimental models from which the entire Dravida style was drawn.

properties.name: Lakshana Devi Temple, Bharmour
properties.style: Himalayan timber (gabled wooden shrine)
properties.summary: Founded by King Meruvarman around 700 CE, this cedar-wood shrine with its deeply carved doorway is among the oldest wooden temples surviving anywhere in the Himalaya. It preserves the timber tradition from which the hill-state pagoda temples later evolved.
sources: Hermann Goetz, Early Wooden Temples of Chamba

properties.name: Kailasanathar Temple, Kanchipuram
properties.style: Dravida (early structural, sandstone)
properties.summary: The first great structural stone temple of the Tamil country, wrapped in a wall of 58 miniature shrines and lion pilasters. Kailasanathar fixes the classic Dravida formula of vimana, mandapa and enclosing prakara that the Cholas would later monumentalise.

properties.name: Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
properties.style: Dravida (early structural, granite)
properties.summary: Standing on the surf line of the Bay of Bengal, this twin-towered granite temple marks the Pallava leap from carving rock to building in dressed stone. Its slender tiered vimanas are the direct ancestors of every later South Indian temple tower.

properties.name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
properties.major_additions: nine-tier eastern gopuram, ranga-mandapa and courts added 1510 under Krishnadevaraya; continuously enlarged 14th-16th c.
properties.style: Dravida (Vijayanagara)
properties.summary: A small 7th-century Shiva shrine that grew into the ceremonial heart of the Vijayanagara empire, crowned by a 50 m gopuram. Uniquely at Hampi it has remained in unbroken worship, letting visitors experience a medieval imperial temple still alive with ritual.

properties.name: Masrur Rock-cut Temples
properties.style: Nagara (monolithic rock-cut)
properties.summary: The only major monolithic rock-cut temple complex of the Himalaya, a cluster of Nagara shikharas hewn from a single sandstone ridge and mirrored in a sacred pool. Masrur shows the northern tower style translated, uniquely, into the carved-mountain idiom of Ellora.

properties.name: Martand Sun Temple
properties.style: Kashmiri (trefoil arches, peristyle court, pyramidal roofs)
properties.summary: Lalitaditya's grand Sun temple, though now a ruin, defines the distinctive Kashmiri school — Gandharan-influenced fluted columns, trefoil doorways and an 84-column courtyard open to the Himalayan sky. It is the most ambitious classical monument of Kashmir.

properties.name: Virupaksha Temple, Pattadakal
properties.style: Dravida (Chalukya; site pairs Nagara and Dravida temples)
properties.dynasty: Chalukya (Queen Lokamahadevi, wife of Vikramaditya II)
properties.summary: Built by a queen to celebrate victory over the Pallavas, this is the largest of Pattadakal's ten temples, where northern and southern styles stand deliberately side by side. The site is the graduation hall of Chalukya architecture and the model for Ellora's Kailasa.

properties.name: Osian Temples (Sachiya Mata & Harihara group)
properties.major_additions: Sachiya Mata temple rebuilt 12th c.; Jain Mahavira temple enlarged 10th-11th c.
properties.style: Maha-Maru / early western Nagara
properties.summary: This desert oasis preserves the earliest group of Hindu and Jain temples in Rajasthan, their balconied walls and ornate toranas defining the Pratihara school. Osian is where the ornament-rich western Indian idiom that later flowered at Khajuraho and Dilwara began.
sources: Dhaky, Encyclopaedia of Indian Temple Architecture

properties.name: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), Ellora
properties.style: Dravida (monolithic rock-cut)
properties.summary: The largest monolithic structure on earth: a complete two-storey Dravida temple, courtyard, gateway and life-size elephants released from the hillside by removing some 200,000 tonnes of rock, top downward. It is the audacious climax of India's rock-cut tradition.

properties.name: Vettuvan Koil, Kalugumalai
properties.style: Dravida (unfinished monolithic rock-cut)
properties.summary: Called 'heaven of the sculptors', this unfinished Pandya monolith was carved from the top down, leaving its exquisitely finished vimana crown rising from raw rock. It uniquely freezes the construction process, revealing exactly how monolithic temples were made.

properties.name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
properties.major_additions: expanded by Chola, Pandya, Hoysala, Vijayanagara and Nayaka rulers; 72 m Rajagopuram completed 1987
properties.style: Dravida (seven concentric prakaras, 21 gopurams)
properties.dynasty: Chola and successive South Indian dynasties
properties.protection: active temple trust (TN HR&CE); UNESCO Asia-Pacific conservation award
properties.summary: The largest functioning temple complex in India, a 63-hectare temple-town of seven concentric walled enclosures that swallowed the city around it. Srirangam demonstrates the final evolutionary stage of the Dravida temple: from single shrine to sacred urbanism.

properties.name: Lakshmana Temple, Khajuraho
properties.style: Nagara (Chandela, panchayatana)
properties.summary: Consecrated c. 954, this is the earliest fully developed Khajuraho temple, its high platform, clustered shikhara and sculpture-saturated walls announcing the mature central Indian Nagara style. Its friezes preview the sensuous exuberance the site is famous for.

properties.name: Mukteshwar Temple, Bhubaneswar
properties.style: Kalinga (early mature deul with torana)
properties.summary: Nicknamed the 'gem of Odishan architecture', this compact 10th-century shrine introduces the sculpted stone torana archway and the fully articulated Kalinga deul-jagamohana pair. It is the stylistic bridge between early Bhubaneswar shrines and the giant Lingaraj.

properties.name: Gommateshwara (Bahubali), Shravanabelagola
properties.major_additions: Mahamastakabhisheka anointing held every 12 years since 981; surrounding bastis 10th-17th c.
properties.style: monolithic colossus with Jain basti complex
properties.summary: The 17.4 m Bahubali, carved from a single granite outcrop atop Vindhyagiri hill in 981, is one of the largest free-standing monolithic statues in the world. With its hilltop bastis it embodies the Jain contribution of colossal open-air sacred sculpture.

properties.name: Lingaraj Temple, Bhubaneswar
properties.major_additions: nata-mandira and bhoga-mandapa added 12th c. under Eastern Gangas
properties.style: Kalinga (rekha deul)
properties.summary: Its 55 m curvilinear tower dominating Bhubaneswar's skyline, Lingaraj is the grandest living monument of the Kalinga school, with the full four-hall axial sequence later repeated at Puri and Konark. Worship has continued here without interruption for a millennium.
sources: K.C. Panigrahi, Archaeological Remains at Bhubaneswar

properties.name: Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur
properties.major_additions: Subrahmanya shrine 17th c. (Nayaka); Amman shrine 13th c. (Pandya)
properties.style: Dravida (imperial Chola)
properties.summary: Completed in 1010, Rajaraja's 'Great Temple' raised a 66 m all-granite vimana capped by an 80-tonne crowning stone — the tallest structure of its age in India. It is the supreme statement of imperial Dravida architecture and Chola engineering.

properties.name: Sun Temple, Modhera
properties.style: Maru-Gurjara (Solanki) with stepped kund
properties.summary: Aligned so the equinox sun strikes its sanctum, Modhera pairs a lace-carved temple and dance hall with a spectacular stepped tank of 108 miniature shrines. It is the Solanki dynasty's finest showcase of the ornate Maru-Gurjara style.

properties.name: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, Khajuraho
properties.style: Nagara (shekhari clustered shikhara)
properties.summary: The climax of the Nagara style: 84 subsidiary turrets cascade up its 31 m shikhara like a rising mountain range, over walls carrying nearly 900 sculptures. Kandariya Mahadeva is the most perfectly composed temple of medieval north India.

properties.name: Dilwara Temples (Vimal Vasahi & Luna Vasahi), Mount Abu
properties.major_additions: Luna Vasahi added 1230 by ministers Vastupala and Tejapala
properties.style: Maru-Gurjara (Jain, white marble)
properties.summary: Behind plain exteriors lie the most virtuosic marble interiors ever carved in India — pendant lotus ceilings so thin they are translucent. Dilwara represents the Maru-Gurjara style, and Jain patronage, at their absolute technical peak.
sources: Dhaky, Encyclopaedia of Indian Temple Architecture

properties.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram (Brihadisvara Temple)
properties.style: Dravida (imperial Chola)
properties.summary: Built by Rajendra I to crown his new capital after his Ganges expedition, its 55 m vimana answers Thanjavur's with a softer, concave curve and some of the finest Chola sculpture, including the famed Chandesha-anugraha panel. It shows the imperial style refined rather than merely repeated.

properties.name: Rani ki Vav, Patan
properties.style: Maru-Gurjara (stepwell as inverted temple)
properties.summary: A queen's memorial stepwell descending seven storeys, lined with over 500 large sculptures of Vishnu's avatars — effectively a temple built upside-down into the earth. It shows Solanki temple art applied to India's unique water architecture.

properties.name: Palitana Temples, Shatrunjaya Hill
properties.major_additions: most of the 800+ shrines rebuilt 16th c. onward after earlier destructions
properties.style: Maru-Gurjara (Jain temple-city)
properties.dynasty: Jain merchant patrons over nine centuries
properties.summary: Over 800 marble temples climb Shatrunjaya hill in fortified clusters, built and rebuilt by Jain merchants for nine hundred years. Palitana is the world's largest temple-city and the ultimate expression of collective, trans-generational temple building.

properties.name: Vadakkunnathan Temple, Thrissur
properties.major_additions: shrines, koothambalam and murals renewed 15th-17th c.; conservation awarded UNESCO prize 2015
properties.style: Kerala (multi-shrine walled kshetra, sloping copper roofs)
properties.summary: Set in a nine-acre walled green at the heart of Thrissur, this Shiva temple is the archetype of the Kerala style — circular and square shrines under tiered timber-and-copper roofs, with a magnificent koothambalam theatre hall. It shows how the monsoon coast evolved its own gabled temple idiom.

properties.name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
properties.major_additions: gopuram rebuilt 14th c. (Vijayanagara)
properties.style: Hoysala (Vesara, stellate plan, soapstone)
properties.summary: Begun in 1117 to mark Vishnuvardhana's victories, Belur's star-planned soapstone temple carries the celebrated madanika bracket figures, carved with jeweller's precision. It opens the Hoysala chapter, where sculpture and architecture fuse completely.
sources: UNESCO WHC (whc.unesco.org/en/list/1670 - Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas)

properties.name: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
properties.style: Hoysala (twin-shrine, soapstone)
properties.summary: The largest Hoysala temple, its twin shrines wrapped in an unbroken 200 m band of friezes — elephants, epics and deities in thousands — often called the most richly sculpted exterior in India. Halebidu is Hoysala art at maximum density.
sources: UNESCO WHC (Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, 2023)

properties.name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
properties.major_additions: nata-mandira and bhoga-mandapa added later 12th-13th c.; kitchen complex among world's largest
properties.style: Kalinga (rekha deul)
properties.protection: active temple trust (Shri Jagannath Temple Administration); state protected
properties.summary: One of Hinduism's four dhams, its 65 m tower presides over the Rath Yatra, the world's most famous chariot festival. Puri shows the Kalinga temple as a living civic institution, feeding tens of thousands daily from its vast kitchens.

properties.name: Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram
properties.style: Dravida (late Chola, nitya-vinoda ornamental mode)
properties.summary: Conceived as 'perpetual entertainment', this compact late-Chola temple features a mandapa shaped as a stone chariot with wheels and singing steps that ring musically. It shows the imperial style turning from colossal scale to exquisite refinement.

properties.name: Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple, Palampet
properties.style: Kakatiya (Vesara; sandbox foundation, floating bricks)
properties.summary: Named after its sculptor Ramappa, this temple pairs mirror-polished basalt bracket figures with a vimana of porous 'floating' bricks light enough to float on water, over earthquake-resistant sandbox foundations. It is the engineering masterpiece of the Kakatiyas, inscribed by UNESCO in 2021.

properties.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai
properties.major_additions: most gopurams, thousand-pillar hall and tank 16th-17th c. under Nayakas (Tirumala Nayaka)
properties.style: Dravida (Nayaka; 14 polychrome gopurams)
properties.summary: A 14-towered temple-city dedicated jointly to goddess Meenakshi and Shiva, its gateway gopurams teeming with thousands of painted stucco figures. Madurai represents the final Dravida phase, when soaring gateways and vast pillared halls eclipsed the central shrine.

properties.name: Konark Sun Temple
properties.major_additions: main deul collapsed by 19th c.; jagamohana sealed and conserved 1903
properties.style: Kalinga (temple as solar chariot)
properties.summary: The entire temple is conceived as the Sun god's chariot, riding on twelve pairs of exquisitely carved stone wheels drawn by seven horses — the wheels doubling as working sundials. Konark is the audacious grand finale of the Kalinga school.

properties.name: Keshava Temple, Somanathapura
properties.style: Hoysala (trikuta, stellate plan)
properties.dynasty: Hoysala (commander Somanatha Dandanayaka under Narasimha III)
properties.summary: The last and most perfectly finished great Hoysala temple: three star-shaped shrines on a single platform, every surface carved in disciplined horizontal bands. Somanathapura closes the Hoysala story as its most complete surviving statement.
sources: UNESCO WHC (Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, 2023)

properties.name: Vittala Temple, Hampi
properties.major_additions: greatly enlarged 1513-1565 under Krishnadevaraya; stone chariot and musical-pillar mandapas 16th c.
properties.style: Dravida (Vijayanagara, composite mandapa style)
properties.summary: The showpiece of Vijayanagara architecture, famous for its granite stone chariot and halls of slender 'musical' pillars that resonate when struck. Vittala displays the empire's signature open composite mandapas at their most theatrical.

properties.name: Ranakpur Adinatha Temple
properties.style: Maru-Gurjara (Jain chaumukha, 1444 carved pillars)
properties.dynasty: Jain merchant Dharna Shah under Rana Kumbha of Mewar
properties.summary: A four-faced marble temple whose forest of 1,444 pillars — no two alike — fills 29 halls under 80 domes with shifting light. Ranakpur proves the Maru-Gurjara tradition still ascendant in the 15th century, at architectural full complexity.

properties.name: Hidimba Devi Temple, Manali
properties.style: Himalayan pagoda (four-tiered timber roofs)
properties.summary: Rising in four timber tiers from a deodar forest, this 1553 shrine encloses a natural rock worshipped as the goddess Hidimba. It is the best-known example of the Himalayan pagoda style, where cedar wood and sloping roofs answer snow instead of sun.

properties.name: Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati
properties.major_additions: rebuilt 1565 on 8th-10th c. remains; shrines added by Ahom kings 17th-18th c.
properties.style: Nilachal (hybrid: hemispherical dome on cruciform base)
properties.summary: The greatest of the Shakti pithas, rebuilt in 1565 in the 'Nilachal' style invented here — a beehive dome over a cruciform plan that became the template for temples across Assam. It anchors the distinctive northeastern chapter of Indian temple building.

properties.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Thiruvananthapuram
properties.major_additions: rebuilt and expanded 1731-1750s under Marthanda Varma; 30 m seven-tier gopuram completed 18th c.
properties.style: Kerala-Dravida fusion
properties.summary: Home of the reclining Padmanabha and famed for its treasure vaults, this temple uniquely fuses a Tamil-style gopuram with Kerala's sloping roofs and colonnades. It records the meeting of the two great southern building traditions on the Malabar coast.

properties.name: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), Amritsar
properties.major_additions: rebuilt 1764 after destruction; marble cladding and gold gilding 1802-1830 under Maharaja Ranjit Singh
properties.style: Sikh (fusion of Indo-Islamic and Rajput idioms)
properties.dynasty: Sikh Gurus (Guru Arjan Dev); Sikh Empire (Ranjit Singh)
properties.summary: Set at the centre of a sacred pool and entered by descending steps, with four doors open to all, the Golden Temple gave Sikhism its own architectural language of domes, chhatris and gilded surfaces. Its layout deliberately inverts the exclusivity of the hilltop shrine.

properties.name: Terracotta Temples of Bishnupur (Shyam Rai & Jor Bangla)
properties.style: Bengal chala-ratna (curved thatch-form roofs, terracotta panels)
properties.summary: In brick-rich, stone-poor Bengal, the Mallas translated the village thatched hut into temple form, curving their cornices and sheathing walls in narrative terracotta plaques of the Krishna legend. Bishnupur is the definitive gallery of this regional style.
sources: UNESCO tentative list: Temples at Bishnupur

properties.name: Sivadol, Sivasagar
properties.style: Ahom (tall shikhara on Nilachal lines, golden kalasha)
properties.dynasty: Ahom (Queen Ambika for King Siva Singha)
properties.summary: Rising 32 m beside the great Borpukhuri tank, Sivadol is claimed as the tallest Shiva temple of its kind in India and the finest monument of the Ahom dynasty. It shows the Assamese dol style at full maturity on the eve of the colonial era.

properties.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Varanasi
properties.major_additions: domes gilded 1839 with gold from Ranjit Singh; Vishwanath Corridor to the Ganga completed 2021
properties.style: late Nagara (Maratha-period rebuild)
properties.dynasty: Rebuilt by Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore (Maratha)
properties.summary: The present temple of Shiva as Lord of Kashi was rebuilt in 1780 by queen Ahilyabai Holkar, emblematic of the great Maratha-era wave of temple restoration across north India. Its gilded spires and new river corridor link medieval piety to 21st-century urban design.

properties.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple, Kolkata
properties.style: Bengal navaratna (nine-spired)
properties.summary: Built by the philanthropist Rani Rashmoni and sanctified by Ramakrishna's ministry, this riverside Kali temple crowns the Bengali navaratna style with nine spires over a colonnaded courtyard of twelve Shiva shrines. It shows temple architecture entering the modern era under new, non-royal patrons.

properties.name: Laxminarayan (Birla) Mandir, Delhi
properties.style: modern Nagara revival (Orissan-inspired)
properties.dynasty: Birla industrialist family (arch. Sris Chandra Chatterjee)
properties.summary: The first of the famous Birla Mandirs, completed in 1939 and opened by Mahatma Gandhi on condition it admit all castes. Its concrete-and-marble revivalist towers announced industrial patronage and social reform as the new forces in Indian temple building.

properties.name: Somnath Temple, Prabhas Patan
properties.major_additions: current temple consecrated 1951 on site of shrines destroyed and rebuilt repeatedly since at least the 10th c.
properties.style: Maru-Gurjara revival (Chaulukya style)
properties.dynasty: Somnath Trust (initiative of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; arch. Prabhashankar Sompura)
properties.summary: Rebuilt after Independence in the Chaulukya style by the hereditary Sompura temple architects, Somnath resurrects a shrine razed many times over a millennium. It stands for the 20th-century revival of classical temple craft as an act of national renewal.

properties.name: Swaminarayan Akshardham, Delhi
properties.style: modern traditional (pink sandstone and marble, shastra-based, no structural steel)
properties.summary: Opened in 2005 after 11,000 artisans revived shastra-prescribed techniques — carving 234 pillars and nine domes without structural steel. Akshardham demonstrates that the full medieval craft tradition can still be mobilised at monumental scale today.

properties.name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Ayodhya
properties.major_additions: consecrated 22 January 2024; upper floors and 732 m parikrama wall completing through 2026
properties.style: Nagara (Gurjara-Chalukya mode, pink Bansi Paharpur sandstone)
properties.dynasty: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (arch. Chandrakant Sompura)
properties.summary: Consecrated in 2024, this three-storey, 161-foot Nagara temple was designed by the Sompura family in the Gurjara-Chalukya idiom, built without steel and engineered for a thousand-year life. It is the newest landmark in the unbroken 2,000-year evolution of the Indian temple.

properties.name: Taj Mahal
properties.builder: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan
properties.summary: The white-marble mausoleum Shah Jahan built for Mumtaz Mahal is the crowning jewel of Mughal architecture and India's most visited monument. Its perfect symmetry, pietra dura inlay and riverside charbagh gardens draw millions each year at sunrise and moonlight viewings.

properties.name: Agra Fort
properties.builder: Mughal emperor Akbar (extended by Shah Jahan)
properties.summary: Akbar's massive red-sandstone citadel on the Yamuna served as the Mughal seat of power before Delhi. Inside are Shah Jahan's marble palaces, including the Musamman Burj where he was imprisoned within sight of the Taj Mahal.

properties.name: Fatehpur Sikri
properties.builder: Mughal emperor Akbar
properties.summary: Akbar's short-lived red-sandstone capital, built to honour the Sufi saint Salim Chishti, was abandoned within decades, leaving a perfectly preserved Mughal ghost city. Highlights include the towering Buland Darwaza, the Panch Mahal and the saint's marble dargah.

properties.name: Churches and Convents of Goa (Basilica of Bom Jesus, Old Goa)
properties.builder: Portuguese colonial administration and religious orders
properties.summary: Old Goa's baroque and Manueline churches, led by the Basilica of Bom Jesus holding the relics of St Francis Xavier, spread Renaissance church art across Asia. The Se Cathedral and Church of St Francis of Assisi complete one of Asia's grandest Christian ensembles.

properties.name: Hampi (Vijayanagara)
properties.builder: Vijayanagara Empire (Sangama to Tuluva dynasties)
properties.summary: The boulder-strewn ruins of Vijayanagara, once among the world's richest cities, sprawl along the Tungabhadra with royal enclosures, elephant stables, stepped tanks and the iconic stone chariot. Sacked in 1565, the vast site is now a magnet for travellers and climbers alike.

properties.name: Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi
properties.builder: Emperor Ashoka (Maurya), enlarged under Shunga and Satavahana rule
properties.summary: Sanchi's Great Stupa, begun by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, is the oldest stone structure in India, ringed by exquisitely carved toranas depicting the Buddha's life. The hilltop complex traces 1,400 years of Buddhist art in one serene setting.

properties.name: Humayun's Tomb
properties.builder: Empress Bega Begum for Mughal emperor Humayun; architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas
properties.summary: The first great garden tomb of the subcontinent, Humayun's red-sandstone and marble mausoleum pioneered the charbagh layout later perfected at the Taj Mahal. Beautifully restored, it anchors a necropolis of over 100 Mughal-era tombs near the Nizamuddin dargah.

properties.name: Qutb Minar and its Monuments
properties.builder: Qutb-ud-din Aibak and Iltutmish (Delhi Sultanate)
properties.summary: The 72.5-metre fluted Qutb Minar, begun in 1192, towers over Delhi's earliest mosque, the Quwwat-ul-Islam, and the rust-free 4th-century Iron Pillar. The complex marks the dawn of Indo-Islamic architecture in India.

properties.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Mountain Railways of India)
properties.builder: British colonial government / Gillanders Arbuthnot & Co.
properties.protection: Indian Railways; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 1999, extended 2005 and 2008)
properties.summary: The 'Toy Train' has climbed from the plains to Darjeeling at 2,200 m since 1881 through loops and zig-zags, including the famous Batasia Loop. Steam-hauled joyrides past tea gardens make it the most beloved of India's three World Heritage mountain railways.

properties.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
properties.builder: British Raj; architect F.W. Stevens
properties.protection: Indian Railways heritage; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2004)
properties.summary: Mumbai's flamboyant Victorian Gothic railway station, completed in 1887 as Victoria Terminus, fuses Gothic Revival with Indian ornament in a riot of turrets, gargoyles and stained glass. It remains one of the busiest working railway stations in the world.

properties.name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
properties.builder: Sultan Mahmud Begada of Gujarat (earlier hill settlements from 8th century)
properties.summary: The only complete, unaltered pre-Mughal Islamic city in India, Champaner was Sultan Mahmud Begada's capital before being abandoned after 1536. Its Jami Masjid blends Hindu and Islamic craftsmanship beneath the sacred Pavagadh hill.

properties.name: Red Fort Complex
properties.builder: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan
properties.summary: Shah Jahan's red-sandstone palace-fortress of Shahjahanabad held the Peacock Throne and remains India's most symbolic monument, where the Prime Minister hoists the flag every Independence Day. Its Diwan-i-Khas and marble pavilions epitomise late Mughal splendour.

properties.name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
properties.builder: Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II
properties.protection: Rajasthan State Archaeology; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2010)
properties.summary: The best preserved of Jai Singh II's five stone observatories, Jaipur's Jantar Mantar includes the Samrat Yantra, the world's largest sundial, accurate to two seconds. Its monumental instruments still track the heavens with naked-eye precision.

properties.name: Chittorgarh Fort (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)
properties.builder: Mori dynasty; expanded by Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar
properties.summary: India's largest fort spreads over a 180-m-high plateau, scarred by three epic sieges and jauhars that made it the ultimate symbol of Rajput honour. Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory), Rana Kumbha's palace and Padmini's water pavilion crown its 13-km ramparts.

properties.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)
properties.builder: Rana Kumbha of Mewar; architect Mandan
properties.summary: Kumbhalgarh's 36-km wall, often called the second longest in the world after the Great Wall of China, snakes over the Aravalli hills guarding Mewar's second capital. It is the birthplace of Maharana Pratap and glows spectacularly during evening light shows.

properties.name: Amber Fort (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)
properties.builder: Raja Man Singh I of the Kachwaha dynasty
properties.protection: Rajasthan State Archaeology; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2013)
properties.summary: The honey-coloured palace-fort of the Kachwaha rajas rises above Maota Lake outside Jaipur, its Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) glittering with thousands of mirrored mosaics. Ramparts link it to Jaigarh Fort, home of the world's largest wheeled cannon.

properties.name: Jaisalmer Fort (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)
properties.builder: Rawal Jaisal, Bhati Rajput dynasty
properties.summary: The golden-sandstone Sonar Qila rising from the Thar Desert is one of the world's few living forts, with thousands still residing in its lanes of havelis, temples and rooftop cafes. At sunset the whole citadel glows like a sandcastle from a fairy tale.

properties.name: Rani-ki-Vav (Queen's Stepwell), Patan
properties.builder: Queen Udayamati of the Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty
properties.summary: Built as an inverted temple to water, this seven-storey stepwell holds over 500 principal sculptures of Vishnu's avatars and celestial maidens. Buried by Saraswati river silt for centuries, its pristine carvings now feature on India's 100-rupee note.

properties.name: Nalanda Mahavihara
properties.builder: Kumaragupta I (Gupta dynasty), patronised by Harsha and the Palas
properties.summary: The world's first great residential university taught Buddhist philosophy, logic and medicine to some 10,000 monks, drawing scholars like Xuanzang from across Asia. Its red-brick monasteries, stupas and shrines flourished for 800 years before destruction around 1200 CE.

properties.name: Capitol Complex, Chandigarh (Le Corbusier)
properties.builder: Le Corbusier for the Government of Punjab / Government of India
properties.protection: Chandigarh Administration; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2016, transnational Le Corbusier serial site)
properties.summary: Le Corbusier's monumental concrete ensemble of the High Court, Secretariat, Legislative Assembly and Open Hand Monument crowns independent India's first planned city. It is India's only modernist World Heritage architecture, visitable on guided tours.

properties.name: Khangchendzonga National Park
properties.builder: Sacred landscape of the Lepcha and Bhutia peoples; park notified 1977
properties.protection: Sikkim Forest Department; UNESCO World Heritage (mixed site, inscribed 2016)
properties.summary: India's only mixed World Heritage site pairs the world's third-highest peak with a living sacred landscape of caves, lakes and monasteries central to Sikkimese Buddhist and Lepcha belief. Trekkers on the Goecha La trail walk beneath Khangchendzonga's guardian summit.

properties.name: Historic City of Ahmadabad
properties.builder: Sultan Ahmad Shah I of Gujarat
properties.protection: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation / ASI monuments; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2017)
properties.summary: India's first World Heritage City preserves 600 years of walled-city life: carved wooden havelis in tight-knit pols, the Bhadra citadel, Sidi Saiyyed's famed jali screens and Jama Masjid. Heritage walks at dawn reveal a living medieval trading town.

properties.name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
properties.builder: British Raj architects and Indian mercantile patrons
properties.protection: Municipal heritage regulations; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2018)
properties.summary: Facing each other across the Oval Maidan stand two waves of Mumbai's ambition: 19th-century Victorian Gothic public buildings like the High Court and university, and the world's second-largest collection of Art Deco apartments and cinemas along Marine Drive.

properties.name: Jaipur City (Walled City)
properties.builder: Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II; architect Vidyadhar Bhattacharya
properties.protection: State/Municipal heritage administration; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2019)
properties.summary: The Pink City's 1727 grid plan, based on Vedic principles, packs in the Hawa Mahal's honeycomb facade, City Palace, bazaars and Jantar Mantar behind rose-coloured ramparts. It is one of South Asia's earliest and finest planned cities.

properties.name: Dholavira: A Harappan City
properties.builder: Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilisation
properties.summary: On an island in the white salt desert of the Rann of Kutch lie the remains of a 5,000-year-old Harappan metropolis famed for its sophisticated stone architecture and cascading water reservoirs. Its ancient signboard bears the world's oldest known large inscription.

properties.name: Santiniketan
properties.builder: Debendranath Tagore and Rabindranath Tagore
properties.protection: Visva-Bharati University / Ministry of Education; UNESCO World Heritage (inscribed 2023)
properties.summary: Rabindranath Tagore transformed his father's ashram into an open-air university where classes meet under mango trees and art, music and internationalism flourish. Murals, sculptures and the poet's homes make it a pilgrimage for lovers of Bengal's cultural renaissance.

properties.name: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty, Charaideo
properties.builder: Ahom dynasty (Tai-Ahom kings)
properties.summary: Grassy pyramid-like burial mounds of Ahom royalty dot the sacred hillocks of Charaideo, the dynasty's first capital, often called the 'Pyramids of Assam'. Inscribed in 2024, they are Northeast India's first cultural World Heritage site.

properties.name: Raigad Fort (Maratha Military Landscapes of India)
properties.builder: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (rebuilt from earlier Rairi fort)
properties.summary: Shivaji's mountaintop capital, where he was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674, commands the Sahyadris from 820 metres, reached today by ropeway or 1,700 steps. Its royal court, market street and the king's samadhi crown the flagship of the 12-fort Maratha Military Landscapes.

properties.name: Gingee Fort (Maratha Military Landscapes of India)
properties.builder: Kon dynasty origins; expanded by Vijayanagara Nayaks, held by Marathas under Rajaram
properties.summary: Called the 'Troy of the East' by the French, Gingee's triple-hill citadel of Rajagiri, Krishnagiri and Chandrayandurg withstood a seven-year Mughal siege sheltering Chhatrapati Rajaram. It is the sole Tamil Nadu component of the Maratha Military Landscapes.

properties.name: Sindhudurg Fort (Maratha Military Landscapes of India)
properties.builder: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj
properties.summary: Built by Shivaji on a rocky island off Malvan with foundations of molten lead, Sindhudurg anchored the pioneering Maratha navy. Boats ferry visitors across turquoise waters to ramparts hiding a rare temple to Shivaji himself.

properties.name: Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath
properties.builder: Emperor Ashoka (Maurya); expanded through Kushan and Gupta periods
properties.summary: Where the Buddha preached his first sermon around 528 BCE, Ashoka raised stupas and the lion-capital pillar that became India's national emblem. The Dhamek Stupa and monastery ruins near Varanasi became India's 45th World Heritage site in July 2026.

properties.name: Golconda Fort
properties.builder: Qutb Shahi dynasty (on earlier Kakatiya and Bahmani fort)
properties.summary: The granite citadel of the Qutb Shahis guarded the diamond markets that produced the Koh-i-Noor and Hope diamonds. Its legendary acoustics let a clap at the gate be heard at the hilltop durbar hall nearly a kilometre away.

properties.name: Charminar
properties.builder: Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
properties.summary: Hyderabad's four-minareted signature monument was raised in 1591 to mark the founding of the new Qutb Shahi capital. Around it swirl the Laad Bazaar's bangle shops and the aromas of the old city's famous street food.

properties.name: Gwalior Fort
properties.builder: Legendary founding by Suraj Sen; Man Mandir Palace by Man Singh Tomar (1486-1516)
properties.summary: Babur reputedly called this sandstone giant 'the pearl amongst fortresses in India'. Its blue-tiled Man Mandir Palace, colossal rock-cut Jain tirthankaras and one of the world's oldest inscriptions of zero make Gwalior a layered thousand-year epic.

properties.name: Mehrangarh Fort
properties.builder: Rao Jodha, Rathore dynasty of Marwar
properties.summary: Rising 120 metres sheer above Jodhpur's blue houses, Mehrangarh is among India's most dramatic forts, its palaces filled with palanquins, howdahs and miniature paintings in a superbly curated museum. Ziplines and evening concerts add modern thrills to Rathore grandeur.

properties.name: Adalaj Stepwell (Adalaj ni Vav)
properties.builder: Queen Rudabai; completed under Sultan Mahmud Begada
properties.summary: Five storeys of intricately carved sandstone descend to cool water in this 1498 stepwell near Ahmedabad, its octagonal shaft blending Solanki and Islamic ornament. Legend ties its beauty to Queen Rudabai's tragic bargain with the sultan who completed it.

properties.name: Bidar Fort
properties.builder: Sultan Ahmad Shah Wali Bahmani
properties.summary: When the Bahmani sultans shifted their capital to Bidar in 1427 they rebuilt this vast fort with Persian-style palaces, the tile-clad Rangin Mahal and a triple moat cut from red laterite. Nearby stand the Bahmani tombs and the medieval Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan.

properties.name: Gol Gumbaz
properties.builder: Mohammed Adil Shah of Bijapur; architect Yaqut of Dabul
properties.summary: The mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah in Vijayapura carries one of the world's largest domes, spanning some 44 metres unsupported. Its whispering gallery repeats the faintest sound seven times around the vast chamber.

properties.name: Vikramashila Mahavihara
properties.builder: King Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty
properties.summary: Founded by Dharmapala around 800 CE as a rival to Nalanda, Vikramashila trained masters of tantric Buddhism including Atisha, who carried its teachings to Tibet. Excavations at Antichak reveal a huge cruciform stupa ringed by 208 monastic cells.

properties.name: Amaravati Mahastupa
properties.builder: Begun under Maurya-era patronage; embellished by the Satavahana and Ikshvaku dynasties
properties.summary: Once among the grandest stupas in the Buddhist world, Amaravati's Mahachaitya was sheathed in limestone reliefs whose 'Amaravati school' shaped Buddhist art across Asia. The serene site and its museum sit beside the Krishna river near the new Andhra capital named for it.

properties.name: Nagarjunakonda
properties.builder: Ikshvaku dynasty (capital Vijayapuri)
properties.summary: The great Buddhist city of the Ikshvakus, with its stupas, monasteries and amphitheatre, was moved block by block to an island museum when the Nagarjuna Sagar dam flooded the valley in 1960. A scenic boat ride now delivers visitors to relics of 3rd-century Andhra.

properties.name: Warangal Fort
properties.builder: Kakatiya rulers Ganapati Deva and Rudrama Devi
properties.summary: Four freestanding Kakatiya Kala Thoranam gateways — now Telangana's state emblem — mark the heart of the 13th-century Kakatiya capital, ringed by earthen and stone walls. The ruined Swayambhu complex scatters exquisite black-basalt sculpture across lawns.

properties.name: Daulatabad (Devagiri) Fort
properties.builder: Yadava king Bhillama V; expanded by Delhi Sultans and Ahmadnagar rulers
properties.summary: The conical hill-fort of Devagiri, briefly Muhammad bin Tughluq's infamous replacement capital for Delhi, is defended by moats, spiralling dark passages and sheer scarps that made it nearly impregnable. The Chand Minar victory tower rises 30 metres within.

properties.name: Shaniwar Wada
properties.builder: Peshwa Baji Rao I
properties.summary: The fortified palace of the Peshwas ruled much of India in the 18th century until an 1828 fire gutted its teak mansions, leaving mighty gates and garden foundations. An evening sound-and-light show retells Pune's Maratha glory and the palace's ghostly legends.

properties.name: Victoria Memorial
properties.builder: British Raj; architect William Emerson
properties.protection: Victoria Memorial Hall Trust, Ministry of Culture
properties.summary: Kolkata's white-marble tribute to Queen Victoria, completed in 1921, blends British and Mughal design beneath a rotating Angel of Victory. Its galleries hold a superb collection of Raj-era paintings, manuscripts and Calcutta history.

properties.name: Gateway of India
properties.builder: British Raj; architect George Wittet
properties.summary: Built to commemorate King George V's 1911 visit, the basalt Indo-Saracenic arch on Mumbai's harbour witnessed the last British troops leave India in 1948. It remains the city's favourite waterfront promenade and the jetty for Elephanta ferries.

properties.name: The Residency, Lucknow
properties.builder: Nawabs Asaf-ud-Daula and Saadat Ali Khan for the British Resident
properties.summary: The shattered, cannonball-pocked ruins of the British Residency stand frozen since the 147-day Siege of Lucknow in 1857, one of the defining episodes of India's First War of Independence. Lawns, a cemetery and a museum make it a hauntingly peaceful memorial.

properties.name: Cellular Jail (Kala Pani)
properties.builder: British colonial government
properties.protection: National Memorial, Andaman and Nicobar Administration
properties.summary: The dreaded 'Kala Pani' penal colony at Port Blair held freedom fighters like Veer Savarkar in 698 solitary cells radiating from a central tower. Now a National Memorial, its nightly sound-and-light show narrates the prisoners' sacrifice.

properties.name: Mandu (Jahaz Mahal and Royal Enclave)
properties.builder: Malwa Sultans Dilawar Khan, Hoshang Shah and Ghiyas-ud-din Khalji
properties.summary: Perched on a monsoon-swept plateau, the deserted Malwa capital charms with the 'ship palace' Jahaz Mahal floating between two lakes, Hoshang Shah's marble tomb (said to have inspired the Taj) and the romance of Baz Bahadur and Rani Roopmati. It is one of India's great Afghan-architecture ensembles.

properties.name: Orchha (Jehangir Mahal and Fort Complex)
properties.builder: Bundela Rajputs; Jehangir Mahal by Raja Bir Singh Deo (c. 1610)
properties.summary: On an island in the Betwa river, Orchha's Bundela palaces mix Rajput and Mughal styles, crowned by the domed Jehangir Mahal built for a single imperial visit. Riverside chhatris (royal cenotaphs) at sunset are among central India's loveliest sights.

properties.name: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri, Sasaram
properties.builder: Sher Shah Suri; architect Mir Muhammad Aliwal Khan
properties.summary: The red-sandstone mausoleum of the Afghan emperor who built the Grand Trunk Road rises from the middle of a lake at Sasaram, a masterpiece of Indo-Afghan architecture sometimes called the 'second Taj Mahal'. Its 37-metre dome was among the largest in India when finished in 1545.

properties.name: Fort St. George, Chennai
properties.builder: British East India Company
