properties.summary: The first English fortress in India (1644) seeded the city of Madras and today houses the Tamil Nadu legislature, a fine colonial museum and St Mary's Church, the oldest Anglican church east of Suez. Clive of India and Elihu Yale both served within its walls.

properties.name: Mattancherry Palace (Dutch Palace), Kochi
properties.builder: Portuguese (gifted to the Raja of Cochin); renovated by the Dutch in 1663
properties.summary: Gifted by the Portuguese to the Cochin royal family and later refurbished by the Dutch, this quadrangular palace shelters some of India's finest Kerala murals depicting the Ramayana in glowing ochres. It sits amid Kochi's spice markets and the historic Jew Town synagogue quarter.

properties.name: Kangra Fort
properties.builder: Katoch dynasty of Trigarta (ancient origins; recorded from early first millennium)
properties.summary: Claimed as one of the oldest forts in India, the Katoch stronghold at the confluence of the Banganga and Manjhi rivers was coveted by Mahmud of Ghazni, Jahangir and Ranjit Singh alike. Earthquake-scarred ramparts and temple courtyards overlook the Dhauladhar range.

properties.name: Leh Palace
properties.builder: King Sengge Namgyal of Ladakh
properties.summary: The nine-storey mud-brick palace of the Namgyal kings looms over Leh's old town like a miniature Potala, abandoned when Dogra forces invaded in the 1830s. Restored by the ASI, its rooftop offers sweeping views of the Indus valley and Stok Kangri.

properties.name: Kangla Fort, Imphal
properties.builder: Meitei kings of Manipur (traditional founding by Nongda Lairen Pakhangba, 33 CE)
properties.protection: Kangla Fort Board, Government of Manipur
properties.summary: The sacred seat of Manipur's Meitei kings for nearly two millennia, Kangla on the Imphal river blends citadel, coronation site and shrine, guarded by the rebuilt Kangla-Sha dragon-lions. It remained the royal capital until the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891.

properties.name: Rang Ghar, Sivasagar
properties.builder: Ahom king Pramatta Singha
properties.summary: Asia's oldest surviving amphitheatre, the two-storey oval Rang Ghar hosted Ahom royalty watching buffalo fights and games during Rongali Bihu. Its boat-shaped roof and rice-and-egg mortar masonry showcase Ahom engineering near the great Sivasagar tank.

properties.name: Ratnagiri Monastery (Odisha Diamond Triangle)
properties.builder: Gupta-era foundation, flourishing under the Bhaumakara dynasty
properties.summary: Crowning a hill above the Birupa river, Ratnagiri was a great Mahayana and Vajrayana monastic university whose exquisitely carved doorway and colossal Buddha heads rival Nalanda. With nearby Udayagiri and Lalitgiri it forms Odisha's Buddhist 'Diamond Triangle'.

properties.name: Hazarduari Palace, Murshidabad
properties.builder: Nawab Nazim Humayun Jah; architect Duncan Macleod
properties.summary: The 'palace of a thousand doors' on the Bhagirathi river recalls Murshidabad's days as Bengal's capital before Plassey, its Italianate halls now an ASI museum of armoury, chandeliers and Nawabi treasures. Some of its 1,000 doors are false, built to confuse intruders.

properties.name: Rakhigarhi
properties.excavated: ASI 1997-2000 (Amarendra Nath); Deccan College 2012-16 (Vasant Shinde); ASI 2022-present (Sanjay Manjul)
properties.key_finds: Largest Harappan city in India (~350-550 ha) with planned streets, drains, fire altars and cemetery. A 2019 ancient-DNA study of a Rakhigarhi skeleton (Shinde et al., Cell) showed no Steppe-pastoralist ancestry, reshaping debates on Harappan origins.
properties.summary: Rakhigarhi village sits atop one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation, bigger than Mohenjo-daro by some estimates. Visitors can walk the excavated mounds among the modern village and see ongoing ASI trenches. A dedicated site museum is being built to display skeletons, jewellery and seals found here.

properties.name: Dholavira
properties.excavated: ASI 1990-2005, 13 field seasons (R.S. Bisht)
properties.key_finds: Fortified Harappan city with unique stone architecture, elaborate water reservoirs and stepwells, and the famous ten-sign Indus 'signboard'. Inscribed a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.
properties.summary: On Khadir island in the Great Rann of Kutch, Dholavira is India's best-preserved Harappan city, with citadel walls, gateways and giant rock-cut reservoirs you can walk through. The on-site museum explains its 1,500-year urban history. Combine it with the White Rann for a spectacular Kutch circuit.

properties.name: Lothal
properties.museum: ASI Archaeological Museum, Lothal; National Maritime Heritage Complex (under construction)
properties.key_finds: Brick-lined basin identified as the world's earliest known dockyard, plus a bead factory, warehouse, seals and a cemetery. Key evidence of Harappan maritime trade with Mesopotamia.
properties.summary: Lothal was a Harappan port town where a massive brick dockyard, warehouses and bead workshops still stand exposed. The site museum displays seals, tools and ornaments, and India's National Maritime Heritage Complex is coming up here. It is an easy day trip from Ahmedabad.
sources: S.R. Rao, Lothal: A Harappan Port Town (ASI Memoirs)

properties.name: Kalibangan
properties.excavated: ASI 1960-1969, 9 seasons (B.B. Lal, B.K. Thapar); first identified by L.P. Tessitori 1917-19
properties.key_finds: The world's earliest ploughed field surface (pre-Harappan), fire altars suggesting ritual practice, and a twin-mound Harappan town on the dried Ghaggar (Saraswati) river. Also yielded earliest evidence of an earthquake recorded archaeologically.
properties.summary: Kalibangan, meaning 'black bangles' after the shards littering its mounds, preserves both an early and a mature Harappan town beside the vanished Ghaggar-Hakra river. Its furrowed pre-Harappan field is a world first. A small ASI museum at the site displays pottery, seals and bangles.
sources: B.B. Lal et al., Excavations at Kalibangan (ASI)

properties.name: Banawali
properties.excavated: Haryana Dept of Archaeology 1974-77 and ASI seasons to 1983-84 (R.S. Bisht)
properties.key_finds: Fortified Harappan town on the Saraswati palaeochannel with a distinctive semi-elliptical plan, a fine terracotta plough model, seals and weights. Shows pre-Harappan, Harappan and Bara-culture phases.
properties.summary: Banawali in Fatehabad district was a walled Harappan town whose streets and houses were traced by R.S. Bisht before he went on to dig Dholavira. The mound survives amid farmland but has no visitor facilities; its terracotta plough is a textbook artefact. Best appreciated via Haryana's museums.
sources: R.S. Bisht, Excavations at Banawali reports

properties.name: Ropar (Rupnagar)
properties.excavated: ASI 1953-55 (Y.D. Sharma); re-examined 1990s
properties.key_finds: First Harappan site excavated in independent India, with a six-period sequence from Harappan through PGW, NBPW, Kushan, Gupta and medieval times. A dog buried with a human in the Harappan cemetery is a famous find.
properties.summary: On the Sutlej at the edge of the Shivaliks, Ropar shows nearly 4,000 years of continuous settlement stacked in one mound. The ASI site museum walks you through every layer, from Indus seals to medieval glazed ware. It pairs well with a visit to nearby Anandpur Sahib.

properties.name: Surkotada
properties.excavated: ASI 1971-72 (J.P. Joshi)
properties.key_finds: Small fortified Harappan settlement with stone-rubble fortification and a citadel-lower town plan. Claimed horse bones (c. 2000 BCE) identified by Sandor Bokonyi remain central to the debated question of the horse in Harappan India.
properties.summary: Surkotada is a compact walled Harappan outpost in eastern Kutch whose stone fortifications are still traceable on the ground. It is famous among archaeologists for its contested horse remains. Remote and little-visited, it suits travellers doing a deep Kutch archaeology circuit.

properties.name: Rangpur
properties.excavated: Trial digs 1934-47 (M.S. Vats, G.S. Ghurye); ASI 1953-56 (S.R. Rao)
properties.key_finds: First Harappan site found in Gujarat; type-site for the post-urban 'Rangpur culture' with Lustrous Red Ware showing how Harappan traditions faded into regional Chalcolithic cultures. Yielded early evidence of rice husk.
properties.summary: Rangpur on the Bhadar river documents what happened after the Indus cities declined, as Harappan pottery slowly transformed into local wares. The site today is an unmarked mound of specialist interest, with its finds housed in museum collections rather than on site.

properties.name: Sinauli
properties.excavated: ASI 2005-06 (D.V. Sharma; 116 burials); ASI 2018-19 (S.K. Manjul)
properties.key_finds: Asia's largest excavated burial site and, in 2018, three copper-decorated 'chariots', coffin burials with anthropomorphic motifs, copper swords and shields of the Ochre Coloured Pottery/late-Harappan horizon (c. 2000 BCE), suggesting an indigenous warrior elite.
properties.summary: A sugarcane-farming village in Baghpat district became world news when full-size chariots and warrior burials nearly 4,000 years old emerged from its fields. The trenches are backfilled and there is nothing developed to see on site; the finds are displayed in Delhi's National Museum and featured in the documentary 'Secrets of Sinauli'.

properties.name: Hastinapura
properties.excavated: ASI 1950-52 (B.B. Lal); renewed ASI work announced 2020s
properties.key_finds: B.B. Lal's landmark dig linked Painted Grey Ware layers (c. 1100-800 BCE) with the Mahabharata tradition and found evidence of a great Ganga flood that matches the epic's account of the capital shifting to Kaushambi.
properties.summary: Hastinapura, the legendary capital of the Kauravas and Pandavas, is where scientific archaeology first met the Mahabharata. The Vidura-ka-Tila mounds rise beside a town rich in Jain temples, as Hastinapur is also sacred to Jains. It makes a rewarding heritage stop north of Meerut.

properties.name: Ahichchhatra
properties.excavated: ASI 1940-44 (K.N. Dikshit, A. Ghosh); ASI 1963-65 (N.R. Banerjee); renewed ASI excavation 2019
properties.key_finds: Capital of Northern Panchala with one of India's longest cultural sequences from PGW to medieval times, a massive brick fortification circuit and terracotta Gupta-period temple plaques (the famous Ganga-Yamuna terracottas now in the National Museum).
properties.summary: Ahichchhatra's vast walled city near Bareilly covers over 180 hectares, its brick ramparts and temple mounds still dominating the fields. Mentioned in the Mahabharata as the Panchala capital, it is also a Jain pilgrimage site for Parshvanatha. The open mounds reward unhurried explorers.

properties.name: Atranjikhera
properties.excavated: Aligarh Muslim University 1962-68 (R.C. Gaur)
properties.key_finds: Classic sequence from Ochre Coloured Pottery through Black-and-Red Ware, Painted Grey Ware and NBPW, with some of the earliest well-dated iron objects and iron-smelting evidence in the Ganga valley (early 1st millennium BCE).
properties.summary: Atranjikhera on the Kali Nadi is a touchstone site for how the Ganga valley moved from copper to iron. It is an unmarked mound with no tourist infrastructure, of interest chiefly to serious archaeology enthusiasts passing through Etah district.

properties.name: Kaushambi
properties.excavated: Allahabad University 1949-66 (G.R. Sharma)
properties.key_finds: Enormous mud ramparts of the Vatsa mahajanapada capital, the Ghoshitarama Buddhist monastery visited by the Buddha, an Ashokan pillar, and a debated 'syenachiti' (eagle-shaped fire altar).
properties.summary: Kaushambi's colossal earthen ramparts still rise up to 20 metres above the Yamuna floodplain an hour from Prayagraj. This was one of the great cities of the Buddha's time, and you can walk the walls, see the Ashokan pillar stump and the Ghoshitarama monastery ruins. Finds fill a gallery of the Allahabad Museum.

properties.name: Rajgir (Rajagriha)
properties.excavated: ASI 1905-06 (John Marshall); ASI 1950 (A. Ghosh); periodic ASI work since
properties.key_finds: Cyclopean stone walls (over 40 km circuit) of the first Magadhan capital, the Ajatashatru fort, Bimbisara's jail, Jivakarama monastery, and sites of the First Buddhist Council at Saptaparni cave.
properties.summary: Ringed by five hills, Rajgir was the capital of Magadha and a favourite resort of the Buddha and Mahavira. Excavated forts, monasteries and the massive cyclopean wall mingle with hot springs, ropeway rides to the Vishwa Shanti Stupa and the ruins of nearby Nalanda. It is one of Bihar's premier heritage destinations.

properties.name: Pataliputra (Kumhrar)
properties.excavated: ASI 1912-15 (D.B. Spooner, funded by Ratan Tata); K.P. Jayaswal Research Institute 1951-55 (A.S. Altekar, V. Mishra)
properties.key_finds: Remains of the Mauryan 80-pillared hypostyle hall with highly polished sandstone pillars, likely part of the imperial palace of Pataliputra described by Megasthenes; also the Arogya Vihara hospital-monastery of Dhanvantari tradition.
properties.summary: At Kumhrar Park in modern Patna lie the buried remains of Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan empire under Chandragupta and Ashoka. A pillar from the great 80-pillared assembly hall is displayed where Greek envoys once marvelled at the city. The landscaped park makes an easy, evocative city stop.
sources: A.S. Altekar & V. Mishra, Kumrahar Excavations report

properties.name: Sisupalgarh
properties.excavated: ASI 1948 (B.B. Lal); UCLA-Deccan College joint project 2005-09 (Monica L. Smith, R.K. Mohanty)
properties.key_finds: One of India's largest and best-preserved early historic fortified cities: a near-perfect square rampart with eight elaborate gateways and a group of monolithic pillars (the 'sixteen pillars'). Geophysical survey revealed dense urban housing for perhaps 20,000-25,000 people.
properties.summary: On Bhubaneswar's outskirts, Sisupalgarh's grand square ramparts and stone gateways enclose a city that flourished around the time of the Kalinga war and Kharavela. You can walk the rampart and see the monolithic pillars at Sola Khamba. Visit along with Dhauli and the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves.
sources: M.L. Smith & R.K. Mohanty project publications

properties.name: Ujjain (Garh Kalika mound)
properties.excavated: ASI 1955-58 (N.R. Banerjee); Vikram University trenches 1964-65 and later
properties.key_finds: Massive mud rampart and moat of ancient Avanti's capital, iron working, NBPW and punch-marked coins showing urbanism from the early first millennium BCE, confirming Ujjayini as one of India's earliest cities and a key mahajanapada capital.
properties.summary: Modern Ujjain, city of the Mahakaleshwar jyotirlinga and the Kumbh Mela, sits beside the huge earthen ramparts of ancient Ujjayini at Garh Kalika. The mound overlooking the Kshipra lets you stand on 2,800 years of urban history in one of India's seven sacred cities.
sources: N.R. Banerjee, ASI excavation summaries (Indian Archaeology - A Review)

properties.name: Eran (Airikina)
properties.excavated: Sagar University 1960-65 and 1984-88 (K.D. Bajpai, S.K. Pandey); ASI conservation ongoing
properties.agency: Sagar University (Dr Hari Singh Gour Univ); ASI
properties.key_finds: Chalcolithic-to-Gupta sequence, thousands of coins, and standing Gupta monuments including the colossal Varaha statue, Vishnu temple and a Budhagupta pillar; also India's earliest dated sati inscription (510 CE).
properties.summary: Eran on the Bina river combines a deep prehistoric mound with spectacular standing Gupta-era temples, including a monumental boar incarnation of Vishnu. Off the beaten track in Sagar district, it rewards travellers interested in the dawn of temple architecture.
sources: K.D. Bajpai & S.K. Pandey, Eran excavation reports

properties.name: Sannati-Kanaganahalli
properties.excavated: ASI 1994-2001 (Kanaganahalli Mahastupa); Ashokan edicts revealed after 1986 temple-floor collapse at Chandralamba temple
properties.key_finds: A Satavahana-period Mahastupa with c. 60 sculpted dome slabs, 250+ Brahmi inscriptions, Ashokan rock edicts, and a unique inscribed stone portrait of Emperor Ashoka himself, labelled 'Raya Asoko'.
properties.summary: On the banks of the Bhima river in Kalaburagi district, Kanaganahalli near Sannati hides one of India's great Buddhist discoveries: the only known labelled portrait of Ashoka. The reassembled stupa sculptures can be seen at the site, which is being developed as a Buddhist circuit destination.

properties.name: Keeladi (Keezhadi)
properties.excavated: ASI 2015-17, 3 seasons (K. Amarnath Ramakrishna, then P.S. Sriraman); TN State Dept of Archaeology 2017-present (10+ phases)
properties.agency: ASI; TN State Dept of Archaeology
properties.key_finds: Urban Sangam-age settlement on the Vaigai with brick structures, ring wells, Tamil-Brahmi inscribed pottery, and 15,000+ artefacts; radiocarbon dates of c. 580 BCE-200 CE pushed the Sangam era centuries earlier and ignited national debate.
properties.summary: Keeladi near Madurai transformed our picture of early Tamil civilisation, revealing a literate, industrious city from the 6th century BCE. The stylish new site museum and the covered excavation trenches make it South India's most talked-about archaeological attraction. Ongoing digs mean there is something new almost every season.

properties.name: Adichanallur
properties.museum: Porunai Museum, Tirunelveli (finds); on-site 'iconic site' museum under development
properties.excavated: Alexander Rea 1899-1905; ASI 2004-05 (T. Satyamurthy); renewed ASI/TNSDA work 2021-24
properties.agency: ASI; TN State Dept of Archaeology
properties.key_finds: One of India's largest Iron Age urn-burial grounds with hundreds of burial urns containing skeletons, bronze objects, gold diadems and early iron; radiocarbon dates of c. 905-696 BCE. Named an 'iconic site' in the 2020 Union Budget.
properties.summary: At Adichanallur on the Thamirabarani, generations of Tamils were laid to rest in great terracotta urns nearly 3,000 years ago. Excavated since the 1870s, it is one of the earliest-known Iron Age cemeteries in South India. The Porunai Museum in nearby Tirunelveli showcases its extraordinary grave goods.

properties.name: Korkai
properties.excavated: TN State Dept of Archaeology 1968-69; TNSDA renewed excavations 2021-present
properties.key_finds: Early Pandyan port and pearl-fishing capital mentioned in Sangam literature and the Periplus; excavations produced Black-and-Red ware, Tamil-Brahmi sherds and a radiocarbon date of c. 785 BCE from deep levels.
properties.summary: Korkai was the pearl port of the early Pandyas, where the Thamirabarani once met the sea before the coastline shifted. Today's quiet village sits on mounds that have yielded some of Tamil Nadu's oldest urban dates. Combine it with Adichanallur and the Porunai Museum on a Thamirabarani valley heritage trail.

properties.name: Gangaikondacholapuram (Maligaimedu palace site)
properties.museum: Maligaimedu Site Museum (TN Dept of Archaeology); ASI sculpture gallery at the temple
properties.excavated: TN State Dept of Archaeology 1980, 1984, 1991, 2009; renewed phases 2021-23 at Maligaimedu
properties.agency: TN State Dept of Archaeology; ASI
properties.key_finds: Burnt-brick foundations of Rajendra Chola I's imperial palace ('Maligaimedu'), with flat roof-tiles, ivory objects, Chinese ceramics, gold-and-copper bracelets and Chola coins, beside the UNESCO-listed Brihadisvara temple.
properties.summary: Rajendra Chola built this capital to celebrate his Ganges expedition, and its great granite temple still soars over the plains. At nearby Maligaimedu, excavations are exposing the brick palace where the Chola emperors actually lived. The pairing of living temple and buried palace makes a perfect Chola day trip from Kumbakonam.

properties.name: Arikamedu
properties.excavated: Jouveau-Dubreuil identification 1937-41; ASI 1945 (R.E.M. Wheeler); French excavations 1947-50 (J.M. Casal); University of Pennsylvania 1989-92 (Vimala Begley)
properties.agency: ASI; French Institute; University of Pennsylvania
properties.key_finds: Indo-Roman trading port with Mediterranean amphorae, Arretine ware, Roman lamps and glass, plus local bead-making industries, proving direct Rome-South India trade in the early centuries CE.
properties.summary: A short ride from Pondicherry's French quarter, Arikamedu is where Roman wine amphorae and Italian tableware were first dug from Indian soil. Wheeler's 1945 excavation here anchored the chronology of South Indian archaeology. Ruins of a later French mission house stand picturesquely over the ancient port mounds.
sources: Vimala Begley, The Ancient Port of Arikamedu

properties.name: Pattanam (Muziris)
properties.museum: Muziris Heritage Project museums, North Paravur-Kodungallur (finds)
properties.excavated: Kerala Council for Historical Research 2007-2015+, 9+ seasons (P.J. Cherian); PAMA Institute later seasons
properties.key_finds: Likely site of the legendary spice port Muziris: a 6-m wharf with bollards and a dugout canoe, tens of thousands of Roman amphora sherds, Mediterranean glass, beads and pepper evidence, dating mainly 100 BCE-300 CE over an Iron Age base.
properties.summary: Beneath a quiet village north of Kochi lie the remains of Muziris, the port that supplied pepper to the Roman Empire. The trenches are backfilled, but the surrounding Muziris Heritage Project links museums, synagogues, forts and boat jetties into Kerala's richest heritage circuit.

properties.name: Brahmagiri
properties.excavated: Mysore Archaeology Dept 1940 (M.H. Krishna); ASI 1947 (R.E.M. Wheeler); later research incl. dating studies 2010s
properties.key_finds: Wheeler's type-sequence from South Indian Neolithic through Megalithic (Iron Age) to Satavahana early historic, anchored by the nearby Ashokan minor rock edicts at Siddapura, the southernmost edicts known for decades.
properties.summary: Brahmagiri in Chitradurga district is where the chronology of South Indian prehistory was first worked out, above a valley where Ashoka's edicts mark the southern reach of the Mauryan empire. Granite hills, megalithic cists and edict shelters make it an atmospheric detour off the Bengaluru-Hospet route.

properties.name: Chandravalli
properties.excavated: Mysore Archaeology Dept 1929-30 (M.H. Krishna); ASI 1947 (R.E.M. Wheeler)
properties.key_finds: Iron Age-to-Satavahana settlement in a scenic valley, yielding Satavahana coins, Roman denarii and russet-coated painted ware; a rock inscription of Kadamba king Mayurasharma adds early historic depth.
properties.summary: Tucked among boulder hills beside Chitradurga's great fort, Chandravalli combines megalithic burials, a painted-pottery settlement and the cave temple of Ankali Mutt. Its lake-and-rockscape setting makes archaeology here feel like a picnic outing.
sources: Karnataka Dept of Archaeology, Museums & Heritage

properties.name: Maski
properties.excavated: Hyderabad Nizam's Archaeology Dept 1935-37; ASI 1954 (B.K. Thapar); Maski Archaeological Research Project surveys 2010-present
properties.key_finds: The 1915 Maski minor rock edict was the first to name 'Devanampiya Asoka' explicitly, proving the identity of Ashoka; excavations revealed Neolithic, Iron Age megalithic and early historic occupation with gold-working links to nearby Hutti mines.
properties.summary: Maski is where the emperor behind the edicts finally got his name, when an inscription discovered here spelled out 'Ashoka' for the first time. The edict shelter on a granite hill and the surrounding prehistoric landscape reward travellers exploring Raichur's little-visited heritage.

properties.name: Hampi (Vijayanagara royal centre)
properties.excavated: ASI and Karnataka Dept excavations 1976-present in the royal centre; Vijayanagara Research Project documentation 1980-2001 (J.M. Fritz, G. Michell)
properties.key_finds: Excavations in the royal enclosure exposed palace basements, the Mahanavami platform surroundings, aqueducts, the great stepped tank (pushkarani) found intact in the 1980s, and thousands of artefacts of the Vijayanagara empire's capital.
properties.summary: Hampi, capital of the Vijayanagara empire and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is India's grandest medieval ruin-field, where excavation continues to uncover palaces and water systems among giant boulders. The perfectly preserved stepped tank in the royal centre is an excavated showpiece. Allow at least two days to explore.

properties.name: Kodumanal
properties.excavated: Tamil University, Thanjavur 1985-90 (K. Rajan); TN State Dept of Archaeology 2018-21
properties.agency: Tamil University; TN State Dept of Archaeology
properties.key_finds: Sangam-age industrial town ('Kodumanam' of Pathitrupathu) on the ancient trade route, with gem-cutting, shell and steel (wootz-type) workshops, megalithic burials and one of the largest hauls of Tamil-Brahmi inscribed potsherds.
properties.summary: Kodumanal on the Noyyal river was a bustling gem-and-steel manufacturing hub 2,300 years ago, exporting to the Roman world via Kerala ports. The site is open farmland today, but its inscribed pottery rewrote the history of literacy in Tamil Nadu.

properties.name: Porunthal
properties.excavated: Pondicherry University 2009-10 (K. Rajan)
properties.key_finds: Megalithic graves whose paddy grains gave AMS dates of c. 490-450 BCE alongside Tamil-Brahmi inscribed pottery, pushing the date of the Tamil-Brahmi script back to the 5th century BCE; also a major glass-bead industry.
properties.summary: At the foot of the Palani hills, Porunthal's burial mounds yielded rice offerings and inscribed pots that pushed Tamil literacy back before Ashoka. It is an open, undeveloped site, but it is a pivotal stop in the story now told in Tamil Nadu's museums.
sources: K. Rajan, Porunthal excavation reports (Pondicherry University)
The Hindu coverage of Porunthal dating

properties.name: Sivakalai (Sivagalai)
properties.excavated: TN State Dept of Archaeology 2019-present
properties.key_finds: Iron Age urn-burial site on the Thamirabarani where paddy from an offering urn was AMS-dated to c. 1155 BCE, prompting Tamil Nadu's 'Porunai civilisation' claims of 3,200-year-old rice agriculture and early iron use.
properties.summary: Sivagalai's burial urns pushed the Thamirabarani valley's story back over three millennia and made national headlines. The active excavation site itself is not developed for visitors, but its finds star in the Porunai Museum at Tirunelveli.

properties.name: Mayiladumparai
properties.excavated: TN State Dept of Archaeology 2021-present (2+ phases)
properties.key_finds: Iron objects dated to c. 2172 BCE (announced 2022), claimed as the earliest Iron Age evidence in India, at a site spanning microlithic, Neolithic and Iron Age phases in Krishnagiri district.
properties.summary: Mayiladumparai made headlines when Tamil Nadu announced 4,200-year-old iron from its trenches, potentially rewriting the timeline of Indian metallurgy. The hillside site is a working excavation rather than a tourist stop, but it anchors the state's new archaeology trail.
sources: The Hindu / Times of India reports on Mayiladumparai iron dating (May 2022)

properties.name: Nagarjunakonda
properties.excavated: ASI 1926-31 (A.H. Longhurst); 1938 (T.N. Ramachandran); massive salvage excavation 1954-60 (R. Subrahmanyam) before Nagarjunasagar dam submergence
properties.key_finds: Capital of the Ikshvaku dynasty (Vijayapuri) with 30+ Buddhist monasteries, a mahachaitya with Buddha relics, an amphitheatre and Brahmanical temples; India's largest salvage archaeology operation relocated key monuments to an island before the valley was flooded.
properties.summary: Reached by boat across the Nagarjunasagar reservoir, Nagarjunakonda island preserves monuments rescued from a drowned Buddhist metropolis associated with the philosopher Nagarjuna. The island museum's sculptures and relics rank among the finest of early South India. The ferry ride itself is half the adventure.
sources: R. Subrahmanyam et al., Nagarjunakonda excavation memoirs

properties.name: Amaravati (Amaravathi Mahastupa)
properties.excavated: Colin Mackenzie surveys 1798 & 1816; Walter Elliot 1845; ASI digs by Alexander Rea 1888-1909; ASI 1958-59 and 1973-74
properties.key_finds: The Mahachaitya, once India's grandest stupa (possibly Ashokan in origin), famed for its limestone relief sculptures of the 'Amaravati school' now split between the site museum, Chennai Government Museum and the British Museum.
properties.summary: Amaravati's great stupa mound and its superb sculpture gallery tell the story of 1,500 years of Buddhism on the Krishna river. Though many carvings travelled to London and Chennai in colonial times, the site museum retains masterpieces of the Amaravati school. The new Andhra capital region has made it easier than ever to visit.
sources: Robert Knox, Amaravati: Buddhist Sculpture from the Great Stupa (British Museum)

properties.name: Vaishali (Basarh-Kolhua)
properties.excavated: ASI 1903-04 (T. Bloch); 1913-14 (D.B. Spooner); K.P. Jayaswal Institute 1958-62 (A.S. Altekar); ASI at Kolhua 1989-96
properties.key_finds: Capital of the Licchavi republic and site of the Buddha's last sermon: excavations exposed Raja Vishal ka Garh (the ancient citadel), a stupa believed to hold the Licchavis' share of Buddha relics (relic casket found 1958-62), the coronation tank, and the intact Ashokan lion pillar at Kolhua.
properties.summary: Vaishali claims fame as the world's first republic and the place where the Buddha announced his coming parinirvana. The unbroken Ashokan lion pillar at Kolhua, the relic stupa and the museum make it a cornerstone of Bihar's Buddhist circuit, an easy drive from Patna across the Ganga.

properties.name: Piprahwa (Kapilavastu)
properties.excavated: W.C. Peppé 1897-98 (relic casket with inscribed vase); ASI 1971-77 (K.M. Srivastava)
properties.key_finds: Stupa yielding inscribed soapstone caskets recording relics 'of the Buddha, the Blessed One, of the Sakyas'; K.M. Srivastava's 1970s dig found further relic caskets and Kushan-period monastery seals reading 'Devaputra Vihara of Kapilavastu', supporting identification with the Buddha's home town.
properties.summary: Piprahwa, near the Nepal border in Siddharthnagar district, is India's candidate for ancient Kapilavastu, where the Buddha grew up as Prince Siddhartha. The brick stupa that yielded bone relics of the Buddha and its quiet monastery ruins offer a moving stop between Lumbini and Shravasti. The 2025 repatriation of the Piprahwa gems returned its treasures to India.
sources: K.M. Srivastava, Excavations at Piprahwa and Ganwaria (ASI)

properties.name: Sringaverapura
properties.excavated: ASI 1977-86 (B.B. Lal)
properties.key_finds: A remarkable 250-m brick water-harvesting tank complex of the Kushana period (c. 1st century BCE-CE) fed by Ganga floodwaters through silting chambers, at a site linked in the Ramayana to Nishad king Guha, where Rama crossed the Ganga.
properties.summary: At Sringaverapura, upstream of Prayagraj, B.B. Lal uncovered one of ancient India's most sophisticated water-engineering works, a three-tank brick system that filtered Ganga floodwater. Pilgrims know the spot as the place where Lord Rama crossed the Ganga during his exile, and the exposed tanks can be visited beside the village.

properties.name: Purana Qila (Indraprastha)
properties.key_finds: Painted Grey Ware sherds (c. 1000 BCE) linking the fort mound to the Mahabharata's Indraprastha, plus an unbroken sequence from Mauryan ring wells through Sunga, Kushan, Gupta, Rajput, Sultanate and Mughal levels, including a Gupta Gajalakshmi terracotta and a 900-year-old Vaikuntha Vishnu.
properties.summary: Delhi's 16th-century Purana Qila sits on a mound that has been inhabited for some 2,500 years and is popularly identified with the Pandavas' Indraprastha. Open excavation trenches beside the ramparts and an on-site museum let you see Delhi's entire timeline in one place, right next to the zoo and India Gate precinct.

properties.name: Vadnagar
properties.excavated: Gujarat State Archaeology 2006-12; ASI 2014-present (Abhijit Ambekar)
properties.agency: ASI; Gujarat State Dept of Archaeology
properties.key_finds: Seven continuous cultural periods over ~2,750 years, from pre-Mauryan through Buddhist monastic phases (a rare elliptical shrine and monastery, visited by Xuanzang) to Solanki and Sultanate-Mughal towns; aDNA from a 2nd-century CE skeleton matches today's Gujarati population.
properties.summary: Vadnagar in north Gujarat has been lived in without a break for over 2,500 years, and its new Archaeological Experiential Museum, built over a live excavation trench, displays more than 5,000 finds. Add the medieval Kirti Toran gateways, Hatkeshwar temple and Sharmishtha lake for a full heritage day in the hometown of PM Narendra Modi.

properties.name: Bandhavgarh (ASI forest explorations)
properties.excavated: ASI documentation 1938; ASI Jabalpur Circle exploration 2022 (Shivakant Bajpai) across 170 sq km of the tiger reserve
properties.key_finds: The 2022 exploration recorded 26 mostly Buddhist rock-cut caves (2nd c. BCE-5th c. CE), 26 temples, votive stupas, water bodies and inscriptions in Brahmi, Shankh-lipi and Nagari naming cities like Mathura and Kaushambi, evidence of an ancient trade route through the forest.
properties.summary: Bandhavgarh is best known for tigers, but its sandstone hills conceal 2,000-year-old man-made caves, a colossal reclining Vishnu and a hilltop fort used into the 20th century. ASI's 2022 rediscoveries inside the reserve made global headlines, and safari routes pass several sculptures and cave clusters.
